moving onto it and returning after. --land [TRUNK] lands it: the trunk
fast-forwarded and pushed and the closing's bookmark deleted, every
check first: the one named, or for a revision the current or nearest
parent bookmark above the trunk, several refused with the list.

-s is required: `b` makes both commits now, `w` the work half with
the agent half left to push, `a` the agent repo alone, unpaired, with
no trailer, and `p` a plain repo with no trailer. -R is optional and
says where. --body is the text, or @PATH to read it from a file.

Usage: vc-x1 commit [OPTIONS] --scope <SCOPE>

Options:
  -r, --revision <REV>
          The commit the description is for: `@` by default, committed as the
          working copy; `@-` or any draft below it is described in place with no
          new commit, its trailer stamped, so a commit made by hand becomes a
          rung's. Not with `--opening` or `--closing`

  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

  -R, --repo <PATH>
          Where: a path in the workspace for `-s b|w`, its root or either repo,
          or the repo itself for `-s p` [default: the current directory]

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

  -s, --scope <SCOPE>
          Which repos, required: `w|work`, `a|agent`, `b|both`, or `p|por`
          
          [possible values: work, agent, both, por]

      --title <STR>
          Commit title, the Conventional Commit line; with `--opening` or
          `--closing` the bare cycle title [default with `--closing`: read from
          the opening]

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --body <STR|@PATH>
          Commit body, the problem and its solutions, or @PATH to read it from a
          file [default with `--closing`: `[closing] body`, or the opening's for
          a single-step cycle]

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

      --closing <BM|REV>
          Close the cycle whose tip this names, a bookmark or a revision, onto
          the trunk, `--land`'s or `[cycle] trunk`: one commit above it is
          finalized in place, more get the closing commit, the merge of the
          trunk and the tip

      --dead-end
          With `--closing`, close the cycle as a dead end: the title ends "
          dead-end closing", always on a closing commit

      --opening [<BOOKMARK>]
          Make the work commit the cycle's opening: " opening" is appended to
          the bare cycle title, and BOOKMARK is created at the work `@-` and
          pushed to `origin` [default: the bare title's slug]

      --skip <SIDE>
          With `--opening`, what it leaves out: `local`, the bookmark is already
          at the work `@-` and is pushed; `remote`, it is created and not
          pushed; `both`, it is only checked. With `--land`, which side of the
          cycle's bookmark is kept: `local`, `remote`, or `both`, none deleted

          Possible values:
          - local:  The bookmark exists at the work `@-` already, so it is not
            created, only pushed
          - remote: The bookmark is created and not pushed
          - both:   The bookmark exists and is neither created nor pushed

      --land [<TRUNK>]
          With `--closing`, land the cycle on TRUNK, the closing's first parent:
          fast-forward it to the closing, push it, and delete the cycle's
          bookmark [default: `[cycle] trunk`, else `main`]

      --bookmark <NAME>
          The bookmark to advance to the work commit, locally, any on the work
          commit's line, at or below it [default: the line's nearest, or
          `--opening`'s]

      --no-advance
          Leave the line's bookmark where it is, rather than advancing it to the
          work commit

      --push
          Push what was committed, over `[commit] push = false`

      --no-push
          Keep the commit local, over `[commit] push`, true when absent

      --dry-run
          Dry run: show what would be done without executing

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

2	
3	The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
4	its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
5	last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
6	commit's copy of the record.

9	
10	### feat: undo takes back the last vc-x1 run
11	
12	Picked from `## Todo` as **undo takes back the last operation** (wink + agent, 2026-10-28), at the
13	opening of **push refuses rewriting the work trunk**, which this opening first carried and gave up
14	for this, wink's call (2026-10-28): undo is the safety net the push and squash rules lean on, so it
15	comes first. Run in the v0.3.1 form, wink's call (2026-10-28): every cycle from now on.
16	
17	#### Problem
18	
19	A vc-x1 write is local and so can be taken back, but only by raw jj, `jj op restore` in each repo,
20	two op logs for `-s b`, the agent-repo's moving with every session write. A `squash-push -s b` that
21	folds hours of uncommitted work into `@-` by mistake and pushes it leaves the work recoverable from
22	the op log and the remote rewritten, and getting both back means finding the right operation in each
23	repo by hand, restoring without clobbering the files on disk, and pushing the bookmark back past a
24	lease that the restore has made stale.
25	
26	#### Solution
27	
28	- Each vc-x1 run records itself in the op log jj already keeps, with no state file to disagree
29	  with it:
30	  - a run is one vc-x1 invocation, and it commits several operations, possibly in both repos
31	  - every operation a run commits carries one attribute, `args`, the key jj-cli keeps its own
32	    command line in, set by jj-lib's `Transaction::set_attribute`, so `jj op log` shows `args:
33	    vc-x1-dev 0.85.16-2+c594f1c06ba1 validate --fast` beside `args: jj diff --stat`
34	  - its value is the banner's program and build, then the arguments, the body left out and the
35	    title kept
36	  - it is set where each transaction starts: `Session::start_tx` and the three that start their
37	    own, the working-copy snapshot and the git HEAD and git refs imports.
38	- `jj op log` is the view of it: vc-x1 adds no reader of its own.
39	- No undo: the cycle stops after the record, a dead end, wink's (2026-10-29), the reasons in the
40	  Deliberation. A mistake is set aside going forward instead, a line's tail abandoned under a
41	  `dead-end-<id>` bookmark and a change reverted by a new commit, **abandon and revert set a mistake
42	  aside** in `TODO.md`.
43	
44	#### Acceptance check
45	
46	`cargo test` passes with tests that:
47	
48	- every write command's operations carry the run's one `args` line, in each repo it touches, the
49	  program and its build first, the title kept and the body left out.
50	
51	#### Deliberation
52	
53	- Undo first, wink's call (2026-10-28): the rules that stop refusing rewrites rest on everything
54	  local being undoable, so the net is built before the rules change. The push material went back
55	  to `## Todo` as **squash-push shows what it takes, and push follows jj**.
56	- The scenario that decided it, wink's (2026-10-28): a `squash-push -s b` folding hours of work by
57	  mistake and pushing it. jj keeps every earlier state, so nothing is lost locally, and the push is
58	  the part with no one-command way back.
59	- The op log is the record, not a file: the attributes travel with the operations, so the last run
60	  is found by reading the log, and what it pushed by comparing the remote-tracking bookmarks before
61	  and after it.
62	- The run record typed, wink's (2026-10-28): the attribute keys an enum and the id an integer, the
63	  strings jj stores made and read in one place, and a value that does not parse is no run of ours.
64	  The id is 128 bits, not 64: a u64 is ample while ids stay in one repo's local op log, but they
65	  will likely leave it, in a trailer, a message, or another engine, and the UUID v7 layout sorts

139:## Suffix scheme
140-
141-The cycle (opening -> commits -> closing, per the [Cycle protocol](../AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol))
142-encodes each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a
143-Preparation**.
144-
145-This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is not
146-a name for a step: a step is identified by its title, and an in-flight ladder rung carries neither a
147-number nor a version (see [Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)).
148-The identifiers below count commits within a phase, and nothing dereferences one.
149-
150-- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
151-- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: the commits between
152-- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)
153-
154-**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0` and
155-starts at `-1` (its first commit). A single-step cycle is one commit, the Close-out, and carries the
156-bare `X.Y.Z` ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
157-needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0`
158-step without renumbering siblings.
159-
160-Disambiguation:
161-
162-- `-10`: commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a Preparation.
163-- `-1.0`: Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final identifier `0`).
164-
165-**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:
166-
167-- `X.Y.Z-3.0`: Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle

e3750ee feat: a hook enforces the shell rules

Working practices forbids masking a command's exit status, and the
agent broke the rule through a whole session with a trailing
`; echo rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}`, since nothing fails when it slips and the
rule is not in the Rules index.

Solution: a PreToolUse hook, `bash-guard.sh`, denies an echo of the
status and a cargo or vc-x1 command piped into a filter without
pipefail. The set carries it with the user's two other hooks and
`hooks.sh` to check, install, and test them, acquaint runs the check,
and the rule becomes one form, the command bare and last, listed in
the index. See details in zCLOSED.md.

07f6336 fix: the fixture builder drives commit

The dr-1 fixture builder drives `push --title --body` and a bare
`squash-push`, forms vc-x1 no longer takes, so the fixture cannot be
built, and nothing noticed, since the tests read a fixture already built
and never run the builder.

Solution: the builder commits with `commit -s b --bookmark` and
squash-pushes with `-s a --yes`, and a test runs it against the binary
the test build makes, so full validation fails the day a command it
drives changes. See details in zCLOSED.md.

## Closed

### fix: the fixture builder drives commit

Not a `## Todo` entry: found at the Land of **feat: vc-x1 commit takes a revision** (2026-10-26),
when full validation on fwlaptop failed for want of `.fixtures/dr-1`.

#### Problem

`support/fixtures/build-dr-1.py` drives `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --yes --title ... --body ...` and
`vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent>`, two forms that went on 2026-10-20 with **feat: vc-x1 commit,
install, and run-dev**, so the dr-1 fixture cannot be built. Nothing noticed, since the fourteen
`dr1_*` tests read a built fixture and never run the builder: 3900x still holds one built on
2026-10-18, and fwlaptop, whose clone has none, is where the build was first needed.

#### Solution

- The builder commits each rung with `vc-x1 commit -s b --bookmark <bookmark>`, and squash-pushes
  the agent repo with `-s a --yes`.
- A test runs the builder against the vc-x1 the test build makes, so a change to the commands it
  drives fails validation the day it is made.

#### Acceptance check

With `.fixtures/` removed, `python3 support/fixtures/build-dr-1.py .fixtures --local` builds the
fixture, and `vc-x1 validate` passes, the fourteen `dr1_*` tests and the new builder test with it.

Result (2026-10-26, fwlaptop): passed. The builder test also fails against the builder as it was,
on `push`'s retired `--title`.

#### Deliberation

- Opened on the unlanded closing: the bookmark is created at the closing of **feat: vc-x1 commit
  takes a revision** rather than at `main`, and Land takes both cycles, wink's call (2026-10-26).
  - The closing stays as pushed, so no published commit is rewritten.
  - Bends [Opening](AGENTS.md#opening)'s bookmark-on-`main`, for this cycle's opening only.

#### Ladder

- [fix: the fixture builder drives commit][f0] (done)

##### fix: the fixture builder drives commit

The builder follows the commands it drives, and a test keeps it following them.

- **dr1_builder_runs_against_this_vc_x1**, in `tests/cli_fixture_builder.rs`, runs
  `build-dr-1.py --local` into its own tempdir with `VC_X1` set to the binary the test build makes,
  and checks that both repos are colocated. It is ignored like the `dr1_*` tests, so full runs it
  and fast does not, at about 3.5 s.
  - `HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` point at the tempdir, by `tests/common`'s `isolate_config`, now
    public, so init's Claude Code symlink lands there and not under the user's home.
  - Spawning `python3` is entry 4 of the spawn register in `clippy.toml`, test fixture setup,
    widened to name it.

does. Installing only from the trunk keeps the rule above, that the plain `vc-x1` is replaced only
by what is on the trunk.

220-resolve in a clone.

222-- The idea: a `vc-x1-run: <id>` trailer on the commits a run makes, so a clone finds a run's
223-  commits by their trailer where it has no op log to read.

Two Todos are moot:

- **undo refuses clone and init runs** (`TODO.md:204`): this would make `undo` refuse to take back a `clone` or `init` run, and mark those runs in `undo --list`.
- **undo across clones** (`TODO.md:214`): this would let one clone find and undo a run made in another, using a `vc-x1-run: <id>` trailer on the run's commits.

Both exist only to refine a `vc-x1 undo` command, and that command was never built: **feat: undo takes back the last vc-x1 run** stopped as a dead end after adding the run record, and **abandon and revert set a mistake aside** replaced it.

One fact in **undo across clones** still holds without undo: the op log is local to `.jj`, so a clone starts with none of the original's operations, while change ids and `ochid:` trailers carry over. **vc-x1 stamps no user, host, or workspace on its operations** may be a better home for that, but I haven't read that entry yet. I'd delete both and move that fact there if it fits.

### The run record misses workspace init

(agent, 2026-10-29) A `clone` run's first operation in each repo, jj-lib's `add workspace
'default'`, carries no run record, since it is made before vc-x1 opens a transaction. The record is
set at four places, `Session::start_tx` and the snapshot and the two git imports, and workspace
init is a fifth. Seen in a fresh `vc-x1-dev clone`, whose other three operations per repo carry
the run.

- Tag it, or treat the operation before a run's first as the run's base, which is what an undo
  restores to either way.
- `init` makes the same operation and is the other case to check.

### vc-x1 stamps no user, host, or workspace on its operations

(agent, 2026-10-29) In `jj op log` raw jj's operations read `wink@3900x default@` and vc-x1's read
`@`, with no user or host, and its snapshots carry no workspace either. In this work-repo 543
operations are raw jj's, 427 vc-x1's with a workspace, and 389 vc-x1's without.

- Set the user and host through jj-lib's settings, as jj-cli does, so vc-x1's operations read as
  jj's own, the run record saying which run made them.
- The snapshot path sets the workspace as the transactions do.
- A missing stamp tells vc-x1's operations from raw jj's today, and is how a stable vc-x1's
  untagged ones were recognized. The run record replaces that test.

### undo refuses clone and init runs

(wink + agent, 2026-10-29) In a fresh clone the one run `undo --list` offers is the clone, and
undoing it would restore each repo to its first operation, no remote and nothing fetched. There is
no state before a `clone` or an `init` worth returning to, and removing the directory is its undo.

- `undo` refuses a run whose command is `clone` or `init`, naming why, and `undo --list` marks it
  or leaves it out.
- For **feat: undo takes back the last vc-x1 run** or a cycle after it.

### undo across clones

(wink + agent, 2026-10-28, confirmed 2026-10-29) The op log is local to `.jj` and never pushed, so a
run made in one clone cannot be listed or undone from another. A fresh `vc-x1-dev clone` of this
pair begins both op logs at the clone, none of the original's operations carried. Commits carry
their change ids, `c594f1c0`, `c1e9e653`, and `de2e9af7` identical in both, so `ochid:` trailers
resolve in a clone.

- The idea: a `vc-x1-run: <id>` trailer on the commits a run makes, so a clone finds a run's
  commits by their trailer where it has no op log to read.
- What a clone could undo is open: the commits and pushes a trailer finds, not the local operations
  only the original saw.

[package]
name = "vc-x1"
version = "0.85.17"
edition = "2024"

# The package name is the installed binary's name and never
# changes: a cycle's validation installs under its own root,
# `--root tmp/dev` in `.vc-config.md`'s `[validate]` lists, so a
# dev build (a suffixed version) never replaces the stable
# `vc-x1` on the PATH. The promotion is the plain `cargo install`
# from `main`. Before 2026-10-20 a cycle renamed the package to
# `vc-x1-dev` instead, guarded by build.rs (chores-16, 0.78.3).

[lints.clippy]
# The process-spawn ban: `Command::new` is disallowed via
# clippy.toml's `disallowed-methods`, and deny (not warn) so a bare
# new spawn site fails `cargo clippy` even without `-D warnings`.
# The documented allowlist lives in clippy.toml.
disallowed_methods = "deny"

[dependencies]
chrono = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["now"] }
clap = { version = "4.6", features = ["derive", "wrap_help"] }
clap_complete = { version = "4.6", features = ["unstable-dynamic"] }
futures = "0.3"
# The gix jj-lib 0.46 resolves (no features of our own): the
# session's lock-contention downcast needs type identity with the
# errors jj-lib returns, and init's bare-repo creation reuses it.
gix = { version = "0.88", default-features = false }
# When raising jj-lib: check whether it now offers the commits a
# remote's bookmarks are on without fetching. If so, `git_command`
# in src/jj/session.rs and its two callers take it, and
# clippy.toml's register entry 6 closes (TODO.md > ## Waiting).
jj-lib = "0.46"
log = { version = "0.4", features = ["std"] }
pollster = "1.0"
# The rng jj-lib's `SecureConfig` takes to mint a repo's config id,
# at jj-lib 0.46's versions so the types are its own, seeded the way
# jj-cli seeds it (src/jj/session.rs `load_repo_config`).
rand = "0.10"
rand_chacha = "0.10"
serde_json = "1"

[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]
libc = "0.2"

input.old_string:
untagged ones were recognized. The run record replaces that test.

### undo refuses clone and init runs

(wink + agent, 2026-10-29) In a fresh clone the one run `undo --list` offers is the clone, and
undoing it would restore each repo to its first operation, no remote and nothing fetched. There is
no state before a `clone` or an `init` worth returning to, and removing the directory is its undo.

- `undo` refuses a run whose command is `clone` or `init`, naming why, and `undo --list` marks it
  or leaves it out.
- For **feat: undo takes back the last vc-x1 run** or a cycle after it.

### undo across clones

(wink + agent, 2026-10-28, confirmed 2026-10-29) The op log is local to `.jj` and never pushed, so a
run made in one clone cannot be listed or undone from another. A fresh `vc-x1-dev clone` of this
pair begins both op logs at the clone, none of the original's operations carried. Commits carry
their change ids, `c594f1c0`, `c1e9e653`, and `de2e9af7` identical in both, so `ochid:` trailers
resolve in a clone.

- The idea: a `vc-x1-run: <id>` trailer on the commits a run makes, so a clone finds a run's
  commits by their trailer where it has no op log to read.
- What a clone could undo is open: the commits and pushes a trailer finds, not the local operations
  only the original saw.

### land lands @- by default

Usage: vc-x1 squash [OPTIONS] --scope <SCOPE>

Options:
  -R, --repo <PATH>
          Where: a path in the workspace for `-s b|w|a`, its root or either
          repo, or the repo itself for `-s p` [default: the current directory]

  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

          Which sides, required: `w|work`, `a|agent`, `b|both`, or `p|por`
          
          [possible values: work, agent, both, por]

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

      --title <STR>
          A new title for the pair's descriptions, with --body

      --body <STR|@PATH>
          A new body, or @PATH to read it from a file, with --title

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

      --yes
          Rewrite a commit already on the trunk's remote, `main@origin`, which
          is refused without it

      --dry-run
          Dry run: show what would be done without executing

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

[package]
name = "vc-x1"
version = "0.85.18"
edition = "2024"

# The package name is the installed binary's name and never
# changes: a cycle's validation installs under its own root,
# `--root tmp/dev` in `.vc-config.md`'s `[validate]` lists, so a
# dev build (a suffixed version) never replaces the stable
# `vc-x1` on the PATH. The promotion is the plain `cargo install`
# from `main`. Before 2026-10-20 a cycle renamed the package to
# `vc-x1-dev` instead, guarded by build.rs (chores-16, 0.78.3).

[lints.clippy]
# The process-spawn ban: `Command::new` is disallowed via
# clippy.toml's `disallowed-methods`, and deny (not warn) so a bare
# new spawn site fails `cargo clippy` even without `-D warnings`.
# The documented allowlist lives in clippy.toml.
disallowed_methods = "deny"

[dependencies]
chrono = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["now"] }
clap = { version = "4.6", features = ["derive", "wrap_help"] }
clap_complete = { version = "4.6", features = ["unstable-dynamic"] }
futures = "0.3"
# The gix jj-lib 0.46 resolves (no features of our own): the
# session's lock-contention downcast needs type identity with the
# errors jj-lib returns, and init's bare-repo creation reuses it.
gix = { version = "0.88", default-features = false }
# When raising jj-lib: check whether it now offers the commits a
# remote's bookmarks are on without fetching. If so, `git_command`
# in src/jj/session.rs and its two callers take it, and
# clippy.toml's register entry 6 closes (TODO.md > ## Waiting).
jj-lib = "0.46"
log = { version = "0.4", features = ["std"] }
pollster = "1.0"
# The rng jj-lib's `SecureConfig` takes to mint a repo's config id,
# at jj-lib 0.46's versions so the types are its own, seeded the way
# jj-cli seeds it (src/jj/session.rs `load_repo_config`).
rand = "0.10"
rand_chacha = "0.10"
serde_json = "1"

[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]
libc = "0.2"

vc-x1 0.85.17+9109352e38fc

Publish a rung's pair: the work commit on its bookmark and the
agent commit on `main`. Push carries no description and writes
none, so what was reviewed is what goes out.

`commit` makes the pair, both commits now (-s b) or the work
half with its trailer naming the agent @ (-s w). Push publishes
the work @-, so new work in @ is left as it is, and it refuses
a work @- with no `ochid:` trailer, which is not a pair's commit.

The halves are independent, each trailer being fixed before
push runs, so -s b is -s a then -s w, the order the pair is
completed in:
  - agent  complete the partner by the state found: fold the
           journal into a committed one, or commit it as the
           partner when pending or the agent repo changed;
           then squash-push main
  - work   restamp the unpublished work commit if its trailer
           does not name the partner, then set and push
           <bookmark>

-s is required: `b` both halves, `a` the agent half, `w` the work
half, `p` a plain repo's @- on its bookmark. -R is optional and
says where. --bookmark is the line's unless named, as a check or
as a new name created at @- and pushed tracked.

-r names another commit, already made, and a name alone goes out
for it, no pair: the one bookmark at it, or --bookmark's, that
bookmark or a new one created there. The working copy and the
root are refused, and so is a REV of several commits.

Every argument is a flag: the old positional is refused, naming
--bookmark or -r, the one it was.

Rerunning is always safe: a half whose work is done finds nothing
to do. A half that fails before its own push restores the repo it
touched via `jj op restore`.

Usage: vc-x1 push [OPTIONS] --scope <SCOPE>

Options:
  -r, --revision <REV>
          The commit to publish, one: `@-` publishes the pair, any other a name
          alone [default: `@-`]

  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --bookmark <NAME>
          The remote's name for it: a bookmark on the line, moved there, one
          already at REV, or a new name, created there [default: the line's
          bookmark, or the one at REV]

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

  -R, --repo <PATH>
          Where: a path in the workspace for `-s b|w|a`, its root or either
          repo, or the repo itself for `-s p` [default: the current directory]

  -s, --scope <SCOPE>
          Which repos, required: `w|work`, `a|agent`, `b|both`, or `p|por`
          
          [possible values: work, agent, both, por]

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

      --step
          Pause between every stage for an interactive approval gate

      --dry-run
          Print the exact commands for every stage without side effects

  -y, --yes
          Pass the `--step` gates without asking

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

I agree with the rule, and yes, it completes that Todo, since `commit --closing --dead-end` already exists and no new command is needed. I couldn't find yesterday's discussion in the transcripts, so this rests on your summary and the Todo's text. Nothing is edited yet.

**Why it fits the dual-repo model:** we think the agent's transcript keeps its reasoning for the work whatever happens to the tree. A dead-end closing explains in the record why that work stopped, while a bare revert leaves that reasoning with no explanation.

**Wording to settle in v0.3.1**
1. **What "agent had no involvement" means:** I'd test for an `ochid:` trailer on the commit being taken back, because a tool can check that. Every `commit -s b` stamps one, so revert ends up covering only hand-made commits and plain repos. That's narrow, but I think it's what you mean.
2. **The clash with **Dead-end cycles defined**:** that section says a dead-end closing "keeps what is worth keeping, reverts the rest". The new rule should say a closing's tree may undo work, and what it forbids is a separate revert commit for the agent's work.

**What happens to the rest of the Todo**
- **`dead-end-<id>` bookmarks:** these go, which also settles the Todo's open naming question. A dead-end closing lands the whole ladder on the trunk, so every `ochid:` still resolves without a permanent bookmark.
- **Draft lines only, trunk fixed forward:** this carries into v0.3.1. Today's squash into 0.85.17 went against it, which the record already notes as a one-commit bend.
- **The agent-repo is never rewound while the agent runs:** this also carries over.
- **Work only a person touched is theirs:** this merges into the revert rule.
- **The reread of **squash-push shows what it takes, and push follows jj**:** this can't be dropped with the Todo. That entry still says local acts need no refusal because undo takes them back, and undo doesn't exist. I'd add a note to that entry saying so, and do the reread when it opens.

**Decision for you:** what happens when one rung in a ladder is wrong but the rungs after it are good? Read strictly, the rule dead-ends the whole cycle, which seems heavy. I recommend allowing a new rung that corrects the mistake and says why in its subsection. That's ordinary work with its reasoning on record, and dead-ending stays for when the cycle's direction is what failed.

If you agree, I'd run this as one single-step cycle: add the section to the v0.3.1 proposal, delete the Todo, and add the note to the squash-push entry.

The plain version: use revert only for commits the agent had no part in, and otherwise close the cycle as a dead end, with a correcting rung allowed for a single bad step. That finishes the Todo with rule text alone.

#### Setting a mistake aside

What the agent made, or a trailer names, is never deleted, so a mistake is set aside going forward
rather than taken back, on a draft line, in this order of preference:

- A correcting rung, for one wrong step in a ladder that is otherwise good: a new rung changes what
  is wrong and says why in its subsection.
- A dead-end closing ([Dead-end cycles defined](#dead-end-cycles-defined)), the preferred way when
  the cycle's direction is what failed. It lands the whole ladder, so every `ochid:` resolves with
  no bookmark kept for it. Its tree may undo the work, since the closing records why.
- A `dead-end-<id>` bookmark, also a solution and not the preferred one, for dropping a line's tail
  while the cycle continues: the tail is kept under that permanent bookmark, pushed so every `ochid:`
  still resolves, the cycle's bookmark moved back to the chosen commit with a leased push, and a
  `commit -s b` on top says what was dropped and why. The `<id>` sorts by time. Open: its form.
- A revert, only when the agent had no involvement in the change, that is its commit carries no
  `ochid:` trailer: a new commit at the tip applies the inverse, never a removal with a rebase of
  what followed, which rewrites published commits into trees no validation saw. Work only a person
  touched and nothing references is theirs, raw `jj undo` included.

The limits on all of them:

- Draft lines only: nothing on the trunk's remote is set aside by these. The trunk is fixed forward
  by a new cycle, and a bad release is marked rather than renamed.
- The agent-repo is never rewound while the agent runs. After `/exit` a rewind is possible, and it
  truncates the transcript, so it is a deliberate act, never a side effect.

##### Why: set aside, and revert last

The dual-repo protocol is why, wink's call (2026-10-29). We think an agent's transcript keeps its
reasoning for a change whatever happens to the tree, so a bare revert of that change leaves the
reasoning with no account of why it stopped, where a rung or a closing gives one. A trailer is the
test because a tool can read it. It overstates involvement when a person commits by `commit -s b`,
the safe side to err on.

#### Warn rather than refuse

- Open, asked

#### Setting a mistake aside

What the agent made, or a trailer names, is never deleted, so a mistake is set aside going forward
rather than taken back, on a draft line, in this order of preference:

- A correcting rung, for one wrong step in a ladder that is otherwise good: a new rung changes what
  is wrong and says why in its subsection.
- A dead-end closing ([Dead-end cycles defined](#dead-end-cycles-defined)), the preferred way when
  the cycle's direction is what failed. It lands the whole ladder, so every `ochid:` resolves with
  no bookmark kept for it. Its tree may undo the work, since the closing records why.
- A `dead-end-<id>` bookmark, also a solution and not the preferred one, for dropping a line's tail
  while the cycle continues: the tail is kept under that permanent bookmark, pushed so every `ochid:`
  still resolves, the cycle's bookmark moved back to the chosen commit with a leased push, and a
  `commit -s b` on top says what was dropped and why. The `<id>` sorts by time. Open: its form.
- A revert, only when the agent had no involvement in the change, that is its commit carries no
  `ochid:` trailer: a new commit at the tip applies the inverse, never a removal with a rebase of
  what followed, which rewrites published commits into trees no validation saw. Work only a person
  touched and nothing references is theirs, raw `jj undo` included.

The limits on all of them:

- Draft lines only: nothing on the trunk's remote is set aside by these. The trunk is fixed forward
  by a new cycle, and a bad release is marked rather than renamed.
- The agent-repo is never rewound while the agent runs. After `/exit` a rewind is possible, and it
  truncates the transcript, so it is a deliberate act, never a side effect.

##### Why: set aside, and revert last

The dual-repo protocol is why, wink's call (2026-10-29). We think an agent's transcript keeps its
reasoning for a change whatever happens to the tree, so a bare revert of that change leaves the
reasoning with no account of why it stopped, where a rung or a closing gives one. A trailer is the
test because a tool can read it. It overstates involvement when a person commits by `commit -s b`,
the safe side to err on.

#### Warn rather than refuse

- Open, asked

[package]
name = "vc-x1"
version = "0.85.17"
edition = "2024"

# The package name is the installed binary's name and never
# changes: a cycle's validation installs under its own root,
# `--root tmp/dev` in `.vc-config.md`'s `[validate]` lists, so a
# dev build (a suffixed version) never replaces the stable
# `vc-x1` on the PATH. The promotion is the plain `cargo install`
# from `main`. Before 2026-10-20 a cycle renamed the package to
# `vc-x1-dev` instead, guarded by build.rs (chores-16, 0.78.3).

[lints.clippy]
# The process-spawn ban: `Command::new` is disallowed via
# clippy.toml's `disallowed-methods`, and deny (not warn) so a bare
# new spawn site fails `cargo clippy` even without `-D warnings`.
# The documented allowlist lives in clippy.toml.
disallowed_methods = "deny"

[dependencies]
chrono = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["now"] }
clap = { version = "4.6", features = ["derive", "wrap_help"] }
clap_complete = { version = "4.6", features = ["unstable-dynamic"] }
futures = "0.3"
# The gix jj-lib 0.46 resolves (no features of our own): the
# session's lock-contention downcast needs type identity with the
# errors jj-lib returns, and init's bare-repo creation reuses it.
gix = { version = "0.88", default-features = false }
# When raising jj-lib: check whether it now offers the commits a
# remote's bookmarks are on without fetching. If so, `git_command`
# in src/jj/session.rs and its two callers take it, and
# clippy.toml's register entry 6 closes (TODO.md > ## Waiting).
jj-lib = "0.46"
log = { version = "0.4", features = ["std"] }
pollster = "1.0"
# The rng jj-lib's `SecureConfig` takes to mint a repo's config id,
# at jj-lib 0.46's versions so the types are its own, seeded the way
# jj-cli seeds it (src/jj/session.rs `load_repo_config`).
rand = "0.10"
rand_chacha = "0.10"
serde_json = "1"

[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]
libc = "0.2"

[package]
name = "vc-x1"
version = "0.85.18"
edition = "2024"

# The package name is the installed binary's name and never
# changes: a cycle's validation installs under its own root,
# `--root tmp/dev` in `.vc-config.md`'s `[validate]` lists, so a
# dev build (a suffixed version) never replaces the stable
# `vc-x1` on the PATH. The promotion is the plain `cargo install`
# from `main`. Before 2026-10-20 a cycle renamed the package to
# `vc-x1-dev` instead, guarded by build.rs (chores-16, 0.78.3).

[lints.clippy]
# The process-spawn ban: `Command::new` is disallowed via
# clippy.toml's `disallowed-methods`, and deny (not warn) so a bare
# new spawn site fails `cargo clippy` even without `-D warnings`.
# The documented allowlist lives in clippy.toml.
disallowed_methods = "deny"

[dependencies]
chrono = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["now"] }
clap = { version = "4.6", features = ["derive", "wrap_help"] }
clap_complete = { version = "4.6", features = ["unstable-dynamic"] }
futures = "0.3"
# The gix jj-lib 0.46 resolves (no features of our own): the
# session's lock-contention downcast needs type identity with the
# errors jj-lib returns, and init's bare-repo creation reuses it.
gix = { version = "0.88", default-features = false }
# When raising jj-lib: check whether it now offers the commits a
# remote's bookmarks are on without fetching. If so, `git_command`
# in src/jj/session.rs and its two callers take it, and
# clippy.toml's register entry 6 closes (TODO.md > ## Waiting).
jj-lib = "0.46"
log = { version = "0.4", features = ["std"] }
pollster = "1.0"
# The rng jj-lib's `SecureConfig` takes to mint a repo's config id,
# at jj-lib 0.46's versions so the types are its own, seeded the way
# jj-cli seeds it (src/jj/session.rs `load_repo_config`).
rand = "0.10"
rand_chacha = "0.10"
serde_json = "1"

[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]
libc = "0.2"

Usage: vc-x1 init [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --target <URL|PATH|NAME>
          What to create: URL, path, or bare NAME.
          
          - URL: `git@host:owner/name(.git)?`, `https://...(.git)?`,
            used as-is, config not consulted.
          - Path: `./X`, `../X`, `/X`, `~/X`, `~`, `.`, `..`, is the

          - Bare NAME: becomes NAME.git, remote resolved via
            `--repo` chain.

#!/bin/bash
# Try a work-only local cycle in a throwaway dual workspace, with HOME isolated.
B=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/wflow
rm -rf "$B"; mkdir -p "$B/home/.config/jj" "$B/remotes"
export HOME=$B/home XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$B/home/.config
printf '[user]\nname = "T"\nemail = "t@example.com"\n' > "$B/home/.config/jj/config.toml"
V="vc-x1 --no-banner"

show() {
  echo "--- work"; jj -R "$1" log --no-graph -r 'all()' -T 'change_id.short(6) ++ " [" ++ bookmarks ++ "] " ++ description.first_line() ++ " | " ++ description.lines().filter(|l| l.starts_with("ochid")).join(",") ++ "\n"' --ignore-working-copy
  echo "--- agent"; jj -R "$1/$2" log --no-graph -r 'all()' -T 'change_id.short(6) ++ " [" ++ bookmarks ++ "] " ++ description.first_line() ++ " | " ++ description.lines().filter(|l| l.starts_with("ochid")).join(",") ++ "\n"' --ignore-working-copy
}

cycle() { # name, how the closing goes
  cd "$B" || exit 1
  $V init --target "./$1" --repo "local=$B/remotes" || { echo init failed; exit 1; }
  cd "$B/$1" || exit 1
  A=$(sed -n 's/^agent = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .vc-config.md)
  echo "agent dir: $A"
  echo j1 > "$A/journal"
  echo a > a; $V commit -s w --opening --skip remote --no-push --title "feat: x" --body "why"
  echo "rc opening=$?"
  echo j2 >> "$A/journal"
  echo b > b; $V commit -s w --no-push --title "feat: rung" --body "rung"
  echo "rc rung=$?"
  echo j3 >> "$A/journal"
  echo "=== before closing"; show . "$A"
  shift; "$@"
  echo "rc closing=$?"
  echo "=== after"; show . "$A"
  echo "--- remote work bookmarks"; git -C "$B/$1" ls-remote origin 2>&1
}

close_local() { $V commit -s w --closing @- --no-push; }
close_land() { $V commit -s w --closing @- --land main --no-push; }

echo "######## A: closing -s w --no-push, then land -s b"
cycle a close_local
cd "$B/a"; A=$(sed -n 's/^agent = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .vc-config.md)
echo "=== land -s w"; $V land -s w --onto main; echo "rc=$?"
echo "=== land -s b dry"; $V land -s b --onto main --dry-run; echo "rc=$?"
echo "=== land -s b"; $V land -s b --onto main; echo "rc=$?"
show . "$A"
echo "=== remote agent main"; git -C "$A" log origin/main --format='%h %s | %b' 2>&1
echo "=== validate-desc"; $V validate-desc 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"

echo; echo "######## B: closing -s w --land"
cycle b close_land

#!/bin/bash
# Try a work-only local cycle in a throwaway dual workspace, with HOME isolated.
B=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/wflow
rm -rf "$B"; mkdir -p "$B/home/.config/jj" "$B/remotes"
export HOME=$B/home XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$B/home/.config
printf '[user]\nname = "T"\nemail = "t@example.com"\n' > "$B/home/.config/jj/config.toml"
V="vc-x1 --no-banner"

show() {
  echo "--- work"; jj -R "$1" log --no-graph -r 'all()' -T 'change_id.short(6) ++ " [" ++ bookmarks ++ "] " ++ description.first_line() ++ " | " ++ description.lines().filter(|l| l.starts_with("ochid")).join(",") ++ "\n"' --ignore-working-copy
  echo "--- agent"; jj -R "$1/$2" log --no-graph -r 'all()' -T 'change_id.short(6) ++ " [" ++ bookmarks ++ "] " ++ description.first_line() ++ " | " ++ description.lines().filter(|l| l.starts_with("ochid")).join(",") ++ "\n"' --ignore-working-copy
}

cycle() { # name, how the closing goes
  cd "$B" || exit 1
  $V init --target "./$1" --repo "local=$B/remotes" || { echo init failed; exit 1; }
  cd "$B/$1" || exit 1
  A=$(sed -n 's/^agent = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .vc-config.md)
  echo "agent dir: $A"
  echo j1 > "$A/journal"
  echo a > a; $V commit -s w --opening --skip remote --no-push --title "feat: x" --body "why"
  echo "rc opening=$?"
  echo j2 >> "$A/journal"
  echo b > b; $V commit -s w --no-push --title "feat: rung" --body "rung"
  echo "rc rung=$?"
  echo j3 >> "$A/journal"
  echo "=== before closing"; show . "$A"
  shift; "$@"
  echo "rc closing=$?"
  echo "=== after"; show . "$A"
  echo "--- remote work bookmarks"; git -C "$B/$1" ls-remote origin 2>&1
}

close_local() { $V commit -s w --closing @- --no-push; }
close_land() { $V commit -s w --closing @- --land main --no-push; }

echo "######## A: closing -s w --no-push, then land -s b"
cycle a close_local
cd "$B/a"; A=$(sed -n 's/^agent = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .vc-config.md)
echo "=== land -s w"; $V land -s w --onto main; echo "rc=$?"
echo "=== land -s b dry"; $V land -s b --onto main --dry-run; echo "rc=$?"
echo "=== land -s b"; $V land -s b --onto main; echo "rc=$?"
show . "$A"
echo "=== remote agent main"; git -C "$A" log origin/main --format='%h %s | %b' 2>&1
echo "=== validate-desc"; $V validate-desc 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"

echo; echo "######## B: closing -s w --land"
cycle b close_land

#!/bin/bash
# Try a work-only local cycle in a throwaway dual workspace, with HOME isolated.
B=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/wflow
rm -rf "$B"; mkdir -p "$B/home/.config/jj"
export HOME=$B/home XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$B/home/.config
printf '[user]\nname = "T"\nemail = "t@example.com"\n' > "$B/home/.config/jj/config.toml"
V="vc-x1 --no-banner"
A=.agent-session

log1() {
  jj -R "$1" log --no-graph -r 'all() ~ root()' --ignore-working-copy -T 'change_id.short(6) ++ " [" ++ bookmarks ++ "] " ++ description.first_line() ++ " | " ++ description.lines().filter(|l| l.starts_with("ochid")).join(",") ++ "\n"'
}
show() { echo "--- work"; log1 .; echo "--- agent"; log1 "$A"; }
remote() {
  echo "--- origin work:"; git ls-remote origin
  echo "--- origin agent:"; git -C "$A" ls-remote origin
}

start() {
  mkdir -p "$B/r-$1"; cd "$B" || exit 1
  $V init --target "./$1" --repo "local=$B/r-$1" >/dev/null || { echo init failed; exit 1; }
  cd "$B/$1" || exit 1
  echo j1 > "$A/journal"
  echo a > a; $V commit -s w --opening --skip remote --no-push --title "feat: x" --body "why" >/dev/null
  echo "rc opening=$?"
  echo j2 >> "$A/journal"
  echo b > b; $V commit -s w --no-push --title "feat: rung" --body "rung" >/dev/null
  echo "rc rung=$?"
  echo j3 >> "$A/journal"
}

echo "######## A: closing -s w --no-push, then land -s b"
start a
remote
$V commit -s w --closing @- --no-push --body "Closes." ; echo "rc closing=$?"
show; remote
echo "=== land -s b"; $V land -s b --onto main >/dev/null; echo "rc land=$?"
show; remote
echo "=== validate-desc"; $V validate-desc -s b; echo "rc=$?"

echo; echo "######## B: closing -s w --land"
start b
$V commit -s w --closing @- --land main --no-push --body "Closes."; echo "rc closing+land=$?"
show; remote

echo; echo "######## C: closing -s w with no --no-push"
start c
$V commit -s w --closing @- --body "Closes."; echo "rc closing=$?"
show; remote

echo; echo "######## D: the agent repo moves mid-cycle, by squash-push -s a"
start d
$V squash-push -s a --yes >/dev/null; echo "rc squash-push=$?"
echo j4 >> "$A/journal"
echo c > c; $V commit -s w --no-push --title "feat: rung2" --body "rung2" >/dev/null; echo "rc rung2=$?"
show
$V commit -s w --closing @- --no-push --body "Closes." >/dev/null; echo "rc closing=$?"
$V land -s b --onto main; echo "rc land=$?"
show
echo "=== validate-desc"; $V validate-desc -s b; echo "rc=$?"

echo; echo "######## E: single commit, opening then closing -s w"
mkdir -p "$B/r-e"; cd "$B"; $V init --target ./e --repo "local=$B/r-e" >/dev/null; cd "$B/e"
echo a > a; $V commit -s w --opening --skip remote --no-push --title "feat: one" --body "why" >/dev/null; echo "rc opening=$?"
$V commit -s w --closing @- --no-push --body "Finalized."; echo "rc closing=$?"
show

#!/bin/bash
# Try a work-only local cycle in a throwaway dual workspace, with HOME isolated.
B=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/wflow
rm -rf "$B"; mkdir -p "$B/home/.config/jj" "$B/remotes"
export HOME=$B/home XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$B/home/.config
printf '[user]\nname = "T"\nemail = "t@example.com"\n' > "$B/home/.config/jj/config.toml"
V="vc-x1 --no-banner"

show() {
  echo "--- work"; jj -R "$1" log --no-graph -r 'all()' -T 'change_id.short(6) ++ " [" ++ bookmarks ++ "] " ++ description.first_line() ++ " | " ++ description.lines().filter(|l| l.starts_with("ochid")).join(",") ++ "\n"' --ignore-working-copy
  echo "--- agent"; jj -R "$1/$2" log --no-graph -r 'all()' -T 'change_id.short(6) ++ " [" ++ bookmarks ++ "] " ++ description.first_line() ++ " | " ++ description.lines().filter(|l| l.starts_with("ochid")).join(",") ++ "\n"' --ignore-working-copy
}

cycle() { # name, how the closing goes
  cd "$B" || exit 1
  $V init --target "./$1" --repo "local=$B/remotes" || { echo init failed; exit 1; }
  cd "$B/$1" || exit 1
  A=$(sed -n 's/^agent = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .vc-config.md)
  echo "agent dir: $A"
  echo j1 > "$A/journal"
  echo a > a; $V commit -s w --opening --skip remote --no-push --title "feat: x" --body "why"
  echo "rc opening=$?"
  echo j2 >> "$A/journal"
  echo b > b; $V commit -s w --no-push --title "feat: rung" --body "rung"
  echo "rc rung=$?"
  echo j3 >> "$A/journal"
  echo "=== before closing"; show . "$A"
  shift; "$@"
  echo "rc closing=$?"
  echo "=== after"; show . "$A"
  echo "--- remote work bookmarks"; git -C "$B/$1" ls-remote origin 2>&1
}

close_local() { $V commit -s w --closing @- --no-push; }
close_land() { $V commit -s w --closing @- --land main --no-push; }

echo "######## A: closing -s w --no-push, then land -s b"
cycle a close_local
cd "$B/a"; A=$(sed -n 's/^agent = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .vc-config.md)
echo "=== land -s w"; $V land -s w --onto main; echo "rc=$?"
echo "=== land -s b dry"; $V land -s b --onto main --dry-run; echo "rc=$?"
echo "=== land -s b"; $V land -s b --onto main; echo "rc=$?"
show . "$A"
echo "=== remote agent main"; git -C "$A" log origin/main --format='%h %s | %b' 2>&1
echo "=== validate-desc"; $V validate-desc 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"

echo; echo "######## B: closing -s w --land"
cycle b close_land

#!/bin/bash
# Try a work-only local cycle in a throwaway dual workspace, with HOME isolated.
B=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/wflow
rm -rf "$B"; mkdir -p "$B/home/.config/jj"
export HOME=$B/home XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$B/home/.config
printf '[user]\nname = "T"\nemail = "t@example.com"\n' > "$B/home/.config/jj/config.toml"
V="vc-x1 --no-banner"
A=.agent-session

log1() {
  jj -R "$1" log --no-graph -r 'all() ~ root()' --ignore-working-copy -T 'change_id.short(6) ++ " [" ++ bookmarks ++ "] " ++ description.first_line() ++ " | " ++ description.lines().filter(|l| l.starts_with("ochid")).join(",") ++ "\n"'
}
show() { echo "--- work"; log1 .; echo "--- agent"; log1 "$A"; }
remote() {
  echo "--- origin work:"; git ls-remote origin
  echo "--- origin agent:"; git -C "$A" ls-remote origin
}

start() {
  mkdir -p "$B/r-$1"; cd "$B" || exit 1
  $V init --target "./$1" --repo "local=$B/r-$1" >/dev/null || { echo init failed; exit 1; }
  cd "$B/$1" || exit 1
  echo j1 > "$A/journal"
  echo a > a; $V commit -s w --opening --skip remote --no-push --title "feat: x" --body "why" >/dev/null
  echo "rc opening=$?"
  echo j2 >> "$A/journal"
  echo b > b; $V commit -s w --no-push --title "feat: rung" --body "rung" >/dev/null
  echo "rc rung=$?"
  echo j3 >> "$A/journal"
}

echo "######## A: closing -s w --no-push, then land -s b"
start a
remote
$V commit -s w --closing @- --no-push --body "Closes." ; echo "rc closing=$?"
show; remote
echo "=== land -s b"; $V land -s b --onto main >/dev/null; echo "rc land=$?"
show; remote
echo "=== validate-desc"; $V validate-desc -s b; echo "rc=$?"

echo; echo "######## B: closing -s w --land"
start b
$V commit -s w --closing @- --land main --no-push --body "Closes."; echo "rc closing+land=$?"
show; remote

echo; echo "######## C: closing -s w with no --no-push"
start c
$V commit -s w --closing @- --body "Closes."; echo "rc closing=$?"
show; remote

echo; echo "######## D: the agent repo moves mid-cycle, by squash-push -s a"
start d
$V squash-push -s a --yes >/dev/null; echo "rc squash-push=$?"
echo j4 >> "$A/journal"
echo c > c; $V commit -s w --no-push --title "feat: rung2" --body "rung2" >/dev/null; echo "rc rung2=$?"
show
$V commit -s w --closing @- --no-push --body "Closes." >/dev/null; echo "rc closing=$?"
$V land -s b --onto main; echo "rc land=$?"
show
echo "=== validate-desc"; $V validate-desc -s b; echo "rc=$?"

echo; echo "######## E: single commit, opening then closing -s w"
mkdir -p "$B/r-e"; cd "$B"; $V init --target ./e --repo "local=$B/r-e" >/dev/null; cd "$B/e"
echo a > a; $V commit -s w --opening --skip remote --no-push --title "feat: one" --body "why" >/dev/null; echo "rc opening=$?"
$V commit -s w --closing @- --no-push --body "Finalized."; echo "rc closing=$?"
show

#!/bin/bash
# Follow-ups on the wflow.sh trial: trailer checks on the landed cases, and closing --land at -s w.
B=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/wflow
export HOME=$B/home XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$B/home/.config
V="vc-x1 --no-banner"
A=.agent-session

for w in a d; do
  cd "$B/$w" || exit 1
  echo "=== $w: validate-desc over the cycle, each side"
  $V validate-desc -s w -r 'main' -n 5; echo "rc=$?"
  $V validate-desc -s a -r 'main' -n 5; echo "rc=$?"
done

echo "=== d: does the first trailer's change exist in the agent repo?"
cd "$B/d" || exit 1
T=$(jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r 'description(glob:"feat: x opening*")' -T 'description' | sed -n 's#^ochid: /.claude/##p')
echo "trailer $T"
jj -R "$A" log --ignore-working-copy --no-graph -r "$T" -T 'change_id.short(6) ++ " visible\n"'; echo "rc=$?"
echo "--- agent Initial commit now holds:"; jj -R "$A" file list --ignore-working-copy -r main-

echo "=== b: closing -s w --land main"
cd "$B/b" || exit 1
$V commit -s w --closing @- --land main --body "Closes."; echo "rc=$?"
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r 'all() ~ root()' -T 'change_id.short(6) ++ " [" ++ bookmarks ++ "] " ++ description.first_line() ++ "\n"'
jj -R "$A" log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r 'all() ~ root()' -T 'change_id.short(6) ++ " [" ++ bookmarks ++ "] " ++ description.first_line() ++ "\n"'
git ls-remote origin

content.text:
Yes, `commit -s w` works for `--opening`, rungs and `--closing`, and every work commit gets the same `ochid:`, but it's only local with the right flags. I recommend the new protocol, with one guard added first: moving the agent repo mid-cycle currently breaks trailers silently. I tested this with the installed 0.85.17 in a throwaway workspace with its own remotes and `HOME`, and your real repos weren't touched.

**What `-s w` actually does**

| Command | Stays local? | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `commit -s w --opening --no-push` | **No** | Dry run says it creates the bookmark and pushes it to `origin`, because `--no-push` doesn't cover the opening's bookmark |
| `commit -s w --opening --skip remote --no-push` | Yes | Bookmark is local, nothing on `origin` |
| `commit -s w --no-push` (a rung) | Yes | Bookmark advances locally |
| `commit -s w --closing @- --no-push` | Yes | Makes the merge closing, or finalizes in place for a one-commit cycle |
| `commit -s w --closing @-` | **No** | Publishes both repos: the agent `main` and the cycle's bookmark |
| `commit -s w --closing @- --land main` | **No, by design** | Lands both repos in one step, and `--land` can't be combined with `--no-push` |

- **`-s w` isn't work-only at push time:** it means the agent half is left for later, and any push it triggers still publishes the pair. Only the flags keep it local.
- **The land step:** `land -s w` is refused, so the end of a cycle is either `land -s b` or `commit -s w --closing @- --land main`. The agent commit is made during the land rather than after it, and the agent repo goes first, so `origin` never holds a trailer naming an unpublished agent commit.
- **Trailers:** in the normal case `validate-desc` passes on both sides, with the opening, rung and closing all naming the one agent commit.

**Thoughts on the protocol**

It suits a cycle whose contents aren't settled. Rungs can be reshaped freely because nothing is published, and the agent repo stops needing a commit per rung. There are three catches:

1. **Moving the agent repo mid-cycle breaks trailers silently.** This is the serious one, and it's the guard I'd add.
   - **What I tested:** I ran `squash-push -s a --yes` between rungs, which folds the agent `@` into `main`. The change the earlier trailers name then no longer exists.
   - **Why nothing catches it:** commit and land both still succeeded, and only `validate-desc` over the range reported `[not found]` on those two commits.
   - **Effect on the rules:** your routine `squash-push -s a` from At rest has to stop while a cycle is open, and the rules need to say so. I'd also make the land refuse, since it can read the whole line's trailers.
2. **The link back from the agent is one-way.** The agent commit's trailer names only the closing, so a work rung reaches the transcript but the transcript reaches only the closing. We think `lookup` from a rung then gets the whole cycle's agent commit rather than that rung's part, but I read that code only briefly and didn't run it. **vc-x1 push: record uncovered work commits (N:1 work<->agent)** already plans one `ochid:` line per commit, which would fix it.
3. **Everything lives on one machine until the land.** Work and transcript have no remote copy, which matters more the longer a cycle runs. Publishing only the work bookmark isn't a clean way around it, because `land -s w`'s refusal exists to stop trailers on `origin` from naming unpublished agent commits.

**What I'd do**
- Fix `--opening --no-push` so it doesn't push the bookmark. That's a bug that can publish something you meant to keep local.
- Add `[commit] push = false` to `.vc-config.md` for this mode, so forgetting a flag can't publish. It wouldn't cover the opening until that fix is in.
- Add the land check, and the At rest exception to the rules.
- For this cycle, make the opening with `commit -s w --opening --skip remote --no-push` and update the bend in the Deliberation to say so. I won't run `squash-push -s a`, and you'd need to hold off on it until the land too.

The opening is still uncommitted, waiting on your review.

The plain version: it works and fits this cycle, but use the exact flags above, and don't squash the agent repo until the land, because nothing warns you if its trailers break.

show() { echo "--- work"; log1 .; if [ -d "$A" ]; then echo "--- agent"; log1 "$A"; fi; }
remote() {

mk() { # name, extra init flags

  mkdir -p "$B/r-$n"; cd "$B" || exit 1

echo "=== land -s p"; $V land -s p --onto main; echo "rc=$?"

show; remote
echo "=== validate-desc agent"; $V validate-desc -s a -r main -n 5; echo "rc=$?"

echo; echo "######## G: dual workspace, closing --land at -s p"
mk g
echo j1 > "$A/journal"
echo a > a; $V commit -s p --opening --skip remote --no-push --title "feat: x" --body "why" >/dev/null; echo "rc opening=$?"

show; remote

echo a > a; $V commit -s p --opening --skip remote --no-push --title "feat: one" --body "why" >/dev/null; echo "rc opening=$?"

show

mk i
echo j1 > "$A/journal"
echo a > a; $V commit -s p --opening --skip remote --no-push --title "feat: x" --body "why" >/dev/null; echo "rc opening=$?"
echo b > b; $V commit -s p --no-push --title "feat: rung" --body "rung" >/dev/null; echo "rc rung=$?"
$V commit -s b --closing @- --land main --body "Closes."; echo "rc=$?"
show; remote
echo "=== validate-desc work"; $V validate-desc -s w -r main -n 5; echo "rc=$?"

echo; echo "######## J: a plain repo"
mk j -s por
echo a > a; $V commit -s p --opening --skip remote --no-push --title "feat: x" --body "why" >/dev/null; echo "rc opening=$?"
echo b > b; $V commit -s p --no-push --title "feat: rung" --body "rung" >/dev/null; echo "rc rung=$?"
$V commit -s p --closing @- --no-push --body "Closes." >/dev/null; echo "rc closing=$?"
remote

show; remote

#!/bin/bash
# Try a cycle at -s p inside a dual workspace, and in a plain repo, HOME isolated.
B=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/wflow3
rm -rf "$B"; mkdir -p "$B/home/.config/jj"
export HOME=$B/home XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$B/home/.config
printf '[user]\nname = "T"\nemail = "t@example.com"\n' > "$B/home/.config/jj/config.toml"
V="vc-x1 --no-banner"
A=.agent-session

log1() {
  jj -R "$1" log --no-graph -r 'all() ~ root()' --ignore-working-copy -T 'change_id.short(6) ++ " [" ++ bookmarks ++ "] p=" ++ parents.len() ++ " " ++ description.first_line() ++ " | " ++ description.lines().filter(|l| l.starts_with("ochid")).join(",") ++ "\n"'
}
show() { echo "--- work"; log1 .; if [ -d "$A" ]; then echo "--- agent"; log1 "$A"; fi; }
remote() {
  echo "--- origin work:"; git ls-remote origin
  if [ -d "$A" ]; then echo "--- origin agent:"; git -C "$A" ls-remote origin; fi
}
mk() { # name, extra init flags
  n=$1; shift
  mkdir -p "$B/r-$n"; cd "$B" || exit 1
  $V init --target "./$n" --repo "local=$B/r-$n" "$@" >/dev/null || { echo init failed; exit 1; }
  cd "$B/$n" || exit 1
}

echo "######## F: dual workspace, the whole cycle at -s p, closing without land"
mk f
echo j1 > "$A/journal"
echo "=== opening dry, only --no-push"; $V commit -s p --opening --no-push --title "feat: x" --body "why" --dry-run; echo "rc=$?"
echo a > a; $V commit -s p --opening --skip remote --no-push --title "feat: x" --body "why"; echo "rc opening=$?"
echo j2 >> "$A/journal"
echo b > b; $V commit -s p --no-push --title "feat: rung" --body "rung"; echo "rc rung=$?"
echo j3 >> "$A/journal"
echo "=== closing"; $V commit -s p --closing @- --no-push --body "Closes."; echo "rc closing=$?"
show; remote
echo "=== land -s p dry"; $V land -s p --onto main --dry-run; echo "rc=$?"
echo "=== land -s p"; $V land -s p --onto main; echo "rc=$?"
show; remote
echo "=== validate-desc work"; $V validate-desc -s w -r main -n 5; echo "rc=$?"
echo "=== then the agent half: commit -s a"
$V commit -s a --title "feat: x" --body "The session of the cycle."; echo "rc=$?"
show; remote
echo "=== validate-desc agent"; $V validate-desc -s a -r main -n 5; echo "rc=$?"

echo; echo "######## G: dual workspace, closing --land at -s p"
mk g
echo j1 > "$A/journal"
echo a > a; $V commit -s p --opening --skip remote --no-push --title "feat: x" --body "why" >/dev/null; echo "rc opening=$?"
echo b > b; $V commit -s p --no-push --title "feat: rung" --body "rung" >/dev/null; echo "rc rung=$?"
$V commit -s p --closing @- --land main --body "Closes."; echo "rc=$?"
show; remote

echo; echo "######## H: dual workspace, one commit, finalized at -s p"
mk h
echo a > a; $V commit -s p --opening --skip remote --no-push --title "feat: one" --body "why" >/dev/null; echo "rc opening=$?"
$V commit -s p --closing @- --no-push --body "Finalized."; echo "rc closing=$?"
show

echo; echo "######## I: mix, -s p rungs then a -s b closing --land"
mk i
echo j1 > "$A/journal"
echo a > a; $V commit -s p --opening --skip remote --no-push --title "feat: x" --body "why" >/dev/null; echo "rc opening=$?"
echo b > b; $V commit -s p --no-push --title "feat: rung" --body "rung" >/dev/null; echo "rc rung=$?"
$V commit -s b --closing @- --land main --body "Closes."; echo "rc=$?"
show; remote
echo "=== validate-desc work"; $V validate-desc -s w -r main -n 5; echo "rc=$?"

echo; echo "######## J: a plain repo"
mk j -s por
echo a > a; $V commit -s p --opening --skip remote --no-push --title "feat: x" --body "why" >/dev/null; echo "rc opening=$?"
echo b > b; $V commit -s p --no-push --title "feat: rung" --body "rung" >/dev/null; echo "rc rung=$?"
$V commit -s p --closing @- --no-push --body "Closes." >/dev/null; echo "rc closing=$?"
remote
$V land -s p --onto main >/dev/null; echo "rc land=$?"
show; remote

Understood, scratch files go in `./tmp` from now on; the rules already said that and I should have followed them. I moved the three trial scripts to `tmp/` and deleted the throwaway workspaces I'd made under `/tmp`.

**`-s p` isn't an option in a dual workspace.** Every `-s p` command was refused before it did anything, with the same error:

```
error: -s p: 'W/f' is the work side of the dual workspace at 'W/f': use `-s w`, or `-s b` for both sides
```

That covers `commit --opening`, a rung, `commit --closing`, `commit --closing --land` and `land -s p`, and it's checked from `.vc-config.md`.

In a real plain repo, the full cycle works and stays local until the land: opening, rung, merge closing, then `land -s p`. None of those commits carry a trailer.

**Using `-s p` here would need a code change:** a way to treat the work-repo as plain despite its config. It would also leave rungs with no `ochid:` at all. The one thing I got from that trial is how an unpaired agent commit looks: `commit -s a` worked, but `validate-desc` reports it as `miss`, "no matching title in other repo".

Compared with `-s w`:
- **`-s w`:** works today, and every rung reaches the transcript through its trailer. Its weakness is that moving the agent repo mid-cycle leaves dangling trailers.
- **`-s p`, if it were allowed:** can't dangle, because there are no trailers to break, but `lookup` would fall back to matching by time for every rung. That's the weakness the **lookup matches a line to its write by content** Todo describes.

I recommend staying with `-s w`, plus the land check from before, since it keeps the links and needs only a small guard. The opening is still uncommitted, waiting on your review.

content.text:
I agree there's a Todo here, but "work" should mean each combination either does something defined or refuses with a reason, because a few can't do anything sensible. `--closing` at `-s a` is one, since the agent repo has no cycle to close.

**The trailer at `-s p`:** you're right that it's trivial and constant for the cycle. But a `-s p` commit with that trailer in a dual workspace is exactly what `-s w --no-push` already makes, so it adds no capability. In a real plain repo there's no agent repo to name, so `p` would mean "trailer" in one place and "no trailer" in the other. I'd keep `p` meaning no partner, and let it run in a dual workspace only as an explicit opt-out with no trailer.

**The real problem is that scope and publishing are tangled:**
- `-s w` says which repos get committed, but any push it triggers publishes both.
- `--no-push` doesn't cover the opening's bookmark.
- `--land` refuses `--no-push`, which makes sense, but it means "local only" has no single spelling.

So I'd make local-only its own setting that works at every scope, one flag or `[commit] push = false`, with the opening's bookmark included.

**Where things stand today**

| | `-s b` | `-s w` | `-s a` | `-s p` plain repo | `-s p` dual workspace |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rung | works | works | works, unpaired | works | refused |
| `--opening` | works | works | refused | works | refused |
| `--closing` | works | works | refused | works | refused |
| `--closing --land` | works | works, publishes both | refused | not run; `land -s p` works | refused |
| `land` | works | refused | refused | works | refused |

The `-s a` bookend refusals come from reading the code and the `land -s a` one from its help text; the rest I ran.

**What I'd put in the Todo**
- **Matrix:** one table of command against scope, each cell saying what it does or why it refuses. It lives in the README's `### Write scopes` table and is checked by a table-driven test, so a new flag can't leave a gap.
- **Rule for refusals:** keep the existing one, that a scope is valid when what it publishes names nothing it leaves unpublished. That rule constrains publishing rather than committing, so every local cell can work and only the push and land cells can refuse.
- **Guard:** the land check for trailers naming an agent change that no longer exists goes here too.
- **Fix:** `--opening --no-push` stops pushing the bookmark.

**Conflict to resolve:** **commit and land take the same scopes** (`TODO.md:272`) already plans for `commit` to drop `-s a`, the opposite of "all variations". It also has `land` taking `-s w` only when the range has no trailers, which refuses the protocol we just tried. I'd fold that entry into the new one and let the matrix decide, keeping `-s a` for rungs since it works and refusing it for bookends.

If you agree, I'll file it as **commit works at every scope, and local-only is its own setting**, replacing that entry, as a rung of **WIP: cleanup**. I'd rank it first in `## Todo`, since this cycle's protocol depends on it.

This shape works, with four things I'd settle as the Todo gets written:

1. **`--local` has to mean really local.** As a plain synonym it inherits today's bug, where `--opening --no-push` still pushes the bookmark. So that fix belongs in the same work, and the Todo should state the promise: nothing leaves the machine.

2. **Contradictory isn't the same as dangerous.** `--land --local` asks for two opposite things, so `--yes` can't resolve it and it should stay a plain error. Combinations with no agreed meaning yet, like `--closing` at `-s a`, need one defined before they can "work". That would leave `--yes` only for combinations that make sense but are risky.

3. **I'd pick error-unless-`--yes` over a warning for the dangerous ones.** A warning goes by unnoticed when an agent is driving, and `--yes` has nothing to override on a warning. There are two things to reconcile:

content.text:
Agreed on the bug: the opening stops pushing under `--no-push`, and `--local` starts out correct.

Keeping `--yes` and `--no-desc-review` separate is the right split, because they answer different questions: "I accept this risk" and "this text has been reviewed". One can't stand in for the other, so a dangerous commit with reviewed text needs only `--yes`.

**Two things this adds or changes:**
- **The gate would be new:** `commit` has no description gate and no `--yes` today. Its help says the description is reviewed before the commit, but that review only happens in conversation, at step 8 of the per-rung flow.
- **`--yes` would mean something different on `push`:** there `--yes` passes every `--step` gate. Across the commands it should mean one thing, or `push`'s should get a different name.

**The main design question is what the gate does without a terminal.** The agent runs `commit` through the Bash tool, where nothing can answer a prompt. It would have to pass `--no-desc-review` every time, so the gate would never fire for the agent, which is the case it most needs to cover. There are two ways out:
- **Prompt at a terminal, refuse without one:** the agent passes `--no-desc-review` only after your go at step 8, and the rules state that. It's simple, but it relies on the agent following the rule, as today, and the flag becomes routine for the agent.
- **Two steps with a token:** `commit --dry-run` prints the description and a short hash of it, and the real commit must pass that hash. That proves the reviewed text is the committed text, and it needs no terminal. It doesn't prove that you were the one who approved it, though, and it's more machinery.

I'd start with the first and write the Todo so the second can be added later. **A local commit pair before every push** in v0.3.1 already reviews the commit itself before it's published, so a mistake in a local commit is cheap to fix, and `--local` could reasonably skip the gate on its own.

**Open:** whether the gate covers `--closing` with no `--body`, where the text comes from the config. I'd say yes, since it's still text you haven't seen for this commit.

You're right: `vc-x1` doesn't prompt for it. I do that review in conversation at step 8 of the per-rung flow, by showing you the title and body and waiting for your go before I run `commit`. The command itself has no gate.

I took your "`--yes` still has a gate on description" to mean a new gate inside `vc-x1`, and my no-terminal concern came from that reading. If you meant the review stays with me, that concern goes away, and so do the token idea and the choice between the two options.

The split then becomes:
- **`--yes`:** a tool flag that gets past `vc-x1`'s guard on dangerous combinations.
- **Description review:** stays a rule for the agent, so `--yes` on a command doesn't excuse me from showing you the description first.
- **`--no-desc-review`:** not needed as a flag, since there's no gate in the tool to skip. If you want to waive the review, you tell me, as you did with "commit and land", and it's recorded as a bend.

I recommend that version; it's simpler, and it keeps the review where it already works.

commit made at the Land. Folds in **commit and land take the same scopes**, which planned to drop
`commit -s a`, the opposite.

  `commit --opening --no-push` still pushes the bookmark, `--skip remote` being what keeps it, and
  that bug is fixed here so `--local` never inherits it. `[commit] push = false` is the same promise
  as a default.

  Write scopes` table and checked by a table-driven test, so a new flag leaves no gap. Goes with
  **docs: each command's -s help names the scopes it takes**, which checks the help against that
  table. Today, by trial on 0.85.17, the `-s a` refusals read from the code and `land`'s help:
  - `b` and `w` take a rung, `--opening`, `--closing`, and `--closing --land`, and `-s w` with
    `--land` or a push publishes both repos.
  - `a` takes a rung, unpaired, and refuses both bookends.
  - `p` takes all of them in a plain repo, and refuses everything in a dual workspace.
  - `land` takes `b` and `p`, and refuses `w` and `a`.
- `-s p` in a dual workspace: `p` stays "no partner", so it works there as an explicit opt-out with
  no trailer. A trailer would make it `-s w --local`, which exists, and a plain repo has no agent
  repo to name.

  error `--yes` cannot pass. A combination with no agreed meaning, `--closing` at `-s a`, gets one
  defined before it works.

  conversation, at [The per-rung flow](AGENTS.md#the-per-rung-flow) step 8, with no gate in the tool,

  push follows jj** retires `squash --yes`, so the two entries agree first.

  - rewriting a commit on the trunk's remote, which `squash` already guards

  `squash-push` closes it, and until then a cycle held local runs no `squash-push -s a`.

  - the rule that a scope is valid when what it publishes names nothing it leaves unpublished,
    which binds publishing and not committing, so every local cell can work
  - `merge` keeps `w` and `p`, a trapezoid being the work-repo's
  - the repo commands keep `a`: `sync`, `squash`, `squash-push`, `push`, `status`, `move-bookmark`,
    `delete-bookmark`, and `validate-desc` act on the agent-repo as a repo of its own and link
    nothing.
- Open: a held-local cycle's agent commit names only the closing, so the transcript reaches the
  rungs only through their own trailers. **vc-x1 push: record uncovered work commits (N:1
  work<->agent)** plans one `ochid:` line per commit. We think `lookup` from a rung gets the whole
  cycle's agent commit, not yet tried.

The second also leaves a moment where a pushed work `main` names an agent commit that isn't published yet, if the land pushes work before `-s a` runs. With `--land --local` nothing is pushed at that step, so that risk only appears if the publish goes in that order.

content.text:
You're right that it should be `/.agent-session/`, and I repeated the wrong one back to you. But it isn't specific to this cycle: `vc-x1` stamps `/.claude/` on every agent trailer today, whatever the directory is called. So all of main carries it, including my 0.85.17 commit.

**Where it comes from**
- **The constant:** `OCHID_BOT_LABEL` in `src/desc_helpers.rs:23` is hard-coded to `"/.claude"`, and its comment says this is deliberate, an opaque label kept so published trailers stay valid.
- **Existing Todo:** **The docs and the code say .claude where they mean the agent-repo directory** (`TODO.md:1593`) already calls changing it a format change to be decided on its own.

**Why it isn't a one-line change**
- **Old trailers would start failing:** `validate_ochid` compares the prefix exactly, so changing the constant makes `validate-desc` flag every published `/.claude/` trailer as a wrong prefix. `fix-desc` would then want to rewrite those commits.
- **Readers have to accept both:** new commits get the configured name, and old `/.claude/` trailers stay valid forever.
- **The name needs a rule:** `[repos] agent` can be an absolute path or sit anywhere, so the label has to be derived from it, probably its last component.

**Decision for you: how to fit this around the current cycle**
- **A small cycle first (recommended):** fix the stamping and the readers, land and install it, then open this cycle. Every commit here then carries `/.agent-session/qrxovvvqxnrq`, as you want. That small cycle's own commit would be the last one stamped `/.claude/`.
- **A rung in this cycle:** the opening and any rungs before the fix would carry `/.claude/` and later ones `/.agent-session/`, so the cycle wouldn't have one consistent trailer unless they were rewritten by hand, which the rules forbid.
- **Build it with `vc-x1-dev`:** this avoids a separate cycle, but the opening would be stamped by a build whose fix isn't committed yet.

Nothing is committed yet, so choosing the first costs nothing. I'd set the opening's edits aside as a patch in `tmp/`, and the small cycle would run `-s b`, landing as usual, with your go at each step. Should I go ahead with that?
