content.text:
I think a URL is the right fix, and the existing design already leans that way. `notes/forks-multi-user.md` sketches this exact form, and **ochid values may be URLs** has been waiting for it since September. It also removes the question of how to derive a label from `[repos] agent`, because the value names the repo itself rather than a local directory. And this one isn't your oversight alone: the code comment defends `/.claude` as deliberate, so it looked settled.

**The form I'd use, in both directions:**
```
ochid: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1.agent-session#qrxovvvqxnrq
ochid: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1#uzkpltwmukvx
```

**What needs deciding**
1. **It won't be a clickable link to the commit.** GitHub only knows SHAs, so the `#<chid>` part just opens the repo's home page. Using a SHA would make it clickable, but SHAs change on every squash and rewrite, and change ids exist to survive that. I'd keep the change id, so the URL says where to look and `vc-x1` does the resolving. A clone keeps change ids, as the undo cycle confirmed.
2. **Local resolution has to come first.** When the URL matches a repo in this workspace by its `origin`, it resolves locally, with no network. Only a URL matching nothing fetches, so normal work stays offline and fast.
3. **Where the URL comes from:** I'd read `origin` at commit time and normalize it to https, so ssh and https clones stamp the same value.
4. **No remote yet:** `init` stamps its cross-links before it creates the remotes, and `adopt` or a local-path remote may have no usable URL. Those cases need a defined fallback, and a `file://` path wouldn't work on another machine. I'd keep the path form for those, with `/.agent-session/<chid>` as the path label.
5. **A renamed repo:** old trailers go stale, and they can't be rewritten without rewriting published history. A small mapping of old URL to new in `.vc-config.md` would cover it. Deleted or private repos are the link-rot problem the note already accepts: the code stays authoritative and only the context is lost.
6. **Old trailers stay as they are forever:** `/.claude/<id>` and `/<id>` remain valid and are never rewritten. `validate_ochid`'s exact prefix check and `fix-desc` both have to learn this, or they'll flag or rewrite all of history.

**How I'd shape the cycle**
- **Readers before writers:** one rung teaches every reader the URL form, a later one starts stamping it. That way no build can write a form it can't read, including across the family's repos on different versions.
- **Readers to change:** `extract_bare_id`, `validate_ochid`, `fix-desc`, `lookup::partner`, the `dr-1` fixture and push's pending-partner check.
- **This cycle's own trailers:** rungs made with the installed binary still get `/.claude/`, until the stamping rung is installed. I'd accept that and let them be the last ones, rather than use unlanded builds to avoid it.
- **Todos it absorbs:**
  - **ochid values may be URLs**
  - **ochid: agent-repo location qualifier**
  - the ochid-label bullet of **The docs and the code say .claude where they mean the agent-repo directory**
- **Agent-files:** `jj.md`'s trailer section and the rules that describe `/.claude/` need updating, so this also touches the v0.3.1 proposal.

**One question for the opening:** should this cycle still run held local, `-s w --no-push`? I'd say yes, since its contents are still settling, and it keeps the same one-agent-commit form you wanted. **commit works at every scope** goes back to `## Todo` with its trials intact.

The plain version: use a URL plus the change id, resolved locally when possible. Expect it not to be clickable, keep old trailers valid, and change the readers before the writers.

### ochid trailers are URLs

(wink + agent, 2026-10-30) `vc-x1` stamps `/.claude/<chid>` on every agent trailer whatever the
directory is called, from the constant `OCHID_BOT_LABEL` in `src/desc_helpers.rs`, so this workspace's
`.agent-session` is never named, and nothing in a published commit says where its partner lives.
Anyone cloning just the work-repo can't resolve the agent side. Wink's decision: fix it correctly,
the trailer a URL in both directions. Folds in **ochid values may be URLs** and **ochid: agent-repo
location qualifier**, and the ochid-label bullet of **The docs and the code say .claude where they
mean the agent-repo directory**. The design is sketched in [Per-user bot repos via URL-shaped
ochid](notes/forks-multi-user.md#per-user-bot-repos-via-url-shaped-ochid).

- The form, the repo's URL and the change id:
  - `ochid: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1.agent-session#qrxovvvqxnrq`
  - `ochid: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1#uzkpltwmukvx`
- The change id and not a SHA: a SHA changes on every squash and rewrite, and a clone keeps change
  ids. So the URL says where to look and `vc-x1` resolves the rest, and it is no clickable link to
  the commit, GitHub knowing only SHAs.
- Resolved locally first: a URL matching a repo of this workspace by its `origin` needs no network,
  and only a URL matching nothing fetches.
- The URL is read from `origin` at commit time and normalized to https, so ssh and https clones stamp
  the same value. Whether `[remote] agent-repo` in `.vc-config.md`, which already names the
  agent-repo's remote, should supply it is to be decided.
- No remote yet, `init`'s cross-links made before the remotes and `adopt` or a local-path remote:
  a fallback is defined, and we think it is the path form, `/.agent-session/<chid>`, the configured
  directory rather than the constant. A `file://` path is no answer, being one machine's.
- A renamed repo leaves its trailers stale, and rewriting them rewrites published history, so a small
  mapping of old URL to new in `.vc-config.md` is the likely answer. A deleted or private repo is the
  link rot the design note accepts: the code stays authoritative and only the context is lost.
- Published trailers stay valid and are never rewritten: `/.claude/<id>` and `/<id>` keep resolving.
  Today `validate_ochid` compares the prefix exactly, so it and `fix-desc` learn this, or they flag
  or rewrite all of history.
- Readers before writers: one rung teaches every reader the URL form, a later one stamps it, so no
  build writes a form it cannot read, across the family's repos on different versions too. The
  readers: `extract_bare_id`, `validate_ochid`, `fix-desc`, `lookup::partner`, the `dr-1` fixture,
  and push's pending-partner check.
- A cycle's own rungs stamped by the installed binary carry `/.claude/` until the stamping rung is
  installed, accepted as the last of them rather than using unlanded builds to avoid it.
- `jj.md`'s trailer section and the rules naming `/.claude/` follow, so **agent-files(proposal):
  v0.3.1** carries the change.
- Beyond a work-repo and its partner: the ARM session of 2026-08-31 made six commits in the sibling
  `vc-x1-messages` clone (`main` at `5cf8aad7`) while its transcript rode vc-x1's agent-repo with no
  work-repo commit to pair with, so nothing links the two histories. A URL-shaped ochid on the
  transcript commit could name the messages-repo commit, the same shape as a pull request whose real
  history lives in another repo.

input.old_string:
### ochid: agent-repo location qualifier

An ochid is workspace-relative (`/.claude/<chid>`), so nothing in a published commit says *where*
the companion agent-repo lives (vc-x1's is `github.com/winksaville/vc-x1.claude`, discoverable only
by convention). Anyone cloning just the work-repo can't resolve agent-side ochids. Design already
sketched in forks-multi-user.md [Per-user bot repos via URL-shaped
ochid](notes/forks-multi-user.md#per-user-bot-repos-via-url-shaped-ochid): URL-shaped trailers, plus
the complementary `.vc-config.md` repo-index form, and resolver dispatch is one rule (URL -> fetch,
else workspace-relative), existing path-form trailers stay the backward-compatible case.
- Cheap first rung: declare the companion's URL once in the committed `.vc-config.md` (no
  trailer-format change, so any work-repo clone then knows where the agent-repo lives). Rides
  naturally with the refactor program's facade-owns-topology stage (agent-repo-location config).
- Link rot + mirroring mitigations are in the same doc section.
- A real case of our own (2026-08-31): the ARM session made six commits in the sibling
  `vc-x1-messages` clone (the read and done marks plus the marked-done revision record, `main`
  at `5cf8aad7`), while its transcript rode vc-x1's agent-repo squash-push with no work-repo
  commit to pair with, so nothing links the two histories. A URL-shaped ochid on the transcript
  commit could have named the messages-repo commit, the same shape as a pull request whose real
  history lives in another repo.

### ochid values may be URLs

(wink, 2026-09-04) An `ochid:` is a side label and a chid, resolvable only inside the workspace
that wrote it. Letting the value be a URL would let a commit point at a counterpart in a repo the
reader holds no checkout of, which is what a family member reading another member's history
needs. Surfaced at the **agent-files(proposal): v0.2.2** close-out, from wink's direction that it
is coming soon, and that cycle's wording was kept side-based rather than path-based so it does not
have to be undone when it arrives.

- The ochid label: trailers are stamped `/.claude/<id>` whatever the directory is called, and
  every published commit carries that spelling, so changing it is a format change, decided on its
  own or ruled out at the opening.

[package]
name = "vc-x1"
version = "0.85.17"
edition = "2024"

# The package name is the installed binary's name and never
# changes: a cycle's validation installs under its own root,
# `--root tmp/dev` in `.vc-config.md`'s `[validate]` lists, so a
# dev build (a suffixed version) never replaces the stable
# `vc-x1` on the PATH. The promotion is the plain `cargo install`
# from `main`. Before 2026-10-20 a cycle renamed the package to
# `vc-x1-dev` instead, guarded by build.rs (chores-16, 0.78.3).

[lints.clippy]
# The process-spawn ban: `Command::new` is disallowed via
# clippy.toml's `disallowed-methods`, and deny (not warn) so a bare
# new spawn site fails `cargo clippy` even without `-D warnings`.
# The documented allowlist lives in clippy.toml.
disallowed_methods = "deny"

[dependencies]
chrono = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["now"] }
clap = { version = "4.6", features = ["derive", "wrap_help"] }
clap_complete = { version = "4.6", features = ["unstable-dynamic"] }
futures = "0.3"
# The gix jj-lib 0.46 resolves (no features of our own): the
# session's lock-contention downcast needs type identity with the
# errors jj-lib returns, and init's bare-repo creation reuses it.
gix = { version = "0.88", default-features = false }
# When raising jj-lib: check whether it now offers the commits a
# remote's bookmarks are on without fetching. If so, `git_command`
# in src/jj/session.rs and its two callers take it, and
# clippy.toml's register entry 6 closes (TODO.md > ## Waiting).
jj-lib = "0.46"
log = { version = "0.4", features = ["std"] }
pollster = "1.0"
# The rng jj-lib's `SecureConfig` takes to mint a repo's config id,
# at jj-lib 0.46's versions so the types are its own, seeded the way
# jj-cli seeds it (src/jj/session.rs `load_repo_config`).
rand = "0.10"
rand_chacha = "0.10"
serde_json = "1"

[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]
libc = "0.2"

Picked from `## Todo`, filed the same day, wink's call (2026-10-30).

#### Problem

(wink + agent, 2026-10-30) `vc-x1` stamps `/.claude/<chid>` on every agent trailer whatever the
directory is called, from the constant `OCHID_BOT_LABEL` in `src/desc_helpers.rs`, so this workspace's
`.agent-session` is never named, and nothing in a published commit says where its partner lives.
Anyone cloning just the work-repo can't resolve the agent side. Wink's decision: fix it correctly,
the trailer a URL in both directions. Folds in **ochid values may be URLs** and **ochid: agent-repo
location qualifier**, and the ochid-label bullet of **The docs and the code say .claude where they
mean the agent-repo directory**. The design is sketched in [Per-user bot repos via URL-shaped
ochid](notes/forks-multi-user.md#per-user-bot-repos-via-url-shaped-ochid).

- The form, the repo's URL and the change id:
  - `ochid: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1.agent-session#qrxovvvqxnrq`
  - `ochid: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1#uzkpltwmukvx`
- The change id and not a SHA: a SHA changes on every squash and rewrite, and a clone keeps change
  ids. So the URL says where to look and `vc-x1` resolves the rest, and it is no clickable link to
  the commit, GitHub knowing only SHAs.
- Resolved locally first: a URL matching a repo of this workspace by its `origin` needs no network,
  and only a URL matching nothing fetches.
- The URL is read from `origin` at commit time and normalized to https, so ssh and https clones stamp
  the same value. Whether `[remote] agent-repo` in `.vc-config.md`, which already names the
  agent-repo's remote, should supply it is to be decided.
- No remote yet, `init`'s cross-links made before the remotes and `adopt` or a local-path remote:
  a fallback is defined, and we think it is the path form, `/.agent-session/<chid>`, the configured
  directory rather than the constant. A `file://` path is no answer, being one machine's.
- A renamed repo leaves its trailers stale, and rewriting them rewrites published history, so a small
  mapping of old URL to new in `.vc-config.md` is the likely answer. A deleted or private repo is the
  link rot the design note accepts: the code stays authoritative and only the context is lost.
- Published trailers stay valid and are never rewritten: `/.claude/<id>` and `/<id>` keep resolving.
  Today `validate_ochid` compares the prefix exactly, so it and `fix-desc` learn this, or they flag
  or rewrite all of history.
- Readers before writers: one rung teaches every reader the URL form, a later one stamps it, so no
  build writes a form it cannot read, across the family's repos on different versions too. The
  readers: `extract_bare_id`, `validate_ochid`, `fix-desc`, `lookup::partner`, the `dr-1` fixture,
  and push's pending-partner check.
- A cycle's own rungs stamped by the installed binary carry `/.claude/` until the stamping rung is
  installed, accepted as the last of them rather than using unlanded builds to avoid it.
- `jj.md`'s trailer section and the rules naming `/.claude/` follow, so **agent-files(proposal):
  v0.3.1** carries the change.
- Beyond a work-repo and its partner: the ARM session of 2026-08-31 made six commits in the sibling
  `vc-x1-messages` clone (`main` at `5cf8aad7`) while its transcript rode vc-x1's agent-repo with no
  work-repo commit to pair with, so nothing links the two histories. A URL-shaped ochid on the
  transcript commit could name the messages-repo commit, the same shape as a pull request whose real
  history lives in another repo.

content.text:
I like this: it's better than stamping at commit time for a local cycle, and it fixes two problems at once. I'm reading `ocid:` as a second trailer holding a URL to the agent commit's SHA, so tell me if you meant something else. The order at land would be:

1. Commit the agent `@`, with one `ochid:` URL per work commit from opening to closing. Their change ids are already known.
2. Rewrite each work commit, adding `ochid:` (the agent's change id) and `ocid:` (the agent's SHA).
3. Push the agent repo first, then the work repo.

**What it solves**
- **Clickable links:** `ocid: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1.agent-session/commit/<sha>` opens the commit, which change ids can't do.
- **Dangling trailers:** rungs carry no trailer until land, so a `squash-push -s a` mid-cycle has nothing to break.
- **The one-way link:** the agent commit names every rung, not just the closing. That's what **vc-x1 push: record uncovered work commits (N:1 work<->agent)** wanted.
- **This cycle's bends:** no more hand-written trailers once land does the stamping, though `vc-x1-dev` would still be needed.

**What it costs**
- **The agent SHA has to stay final, and today it doesn't.** After the land, your `squash-push -s a` folds the session's tail into that agent commit, which changes its SHA and breaks every `ocid:`, while `ochid:` survives. So the tail would need to go into a new commit instead of being folded. That changes At rest, and it's the biggest catch.
- **The link is one-way by necessity.** A work SHA depends on a description holding the agent SHA, so the agent commit can only name work commits by change id. That seems fine, since the transcript just points at the rungs.
- **Land rewrites what you reviewed.** Only descriptions change, but every work SHA changes. Land should check the trees are identical before and after. The candidate flow in v0.3.1, which uses `cmp` to show the tested binary is the landed one, also breaks if a build embeds its commit id, because the id it embedded no longer exists after the rewrite.
- **It only works on an unpublished ladder.** If the cycle's bookmark was pushed, land should refuse or need `--yes`. Cycles run at `-s b` keep stamping per commit, so there are two modes for readers to accept.
- **Failure partway:** if the agent push succeeds and the work push fails, a retry has to find the agent commit already made. Change ids make that detectable, but it needs a test.
- **`push` today refuses a work `@-` with no trailer:** that has to be relaxed for this mode.
- **`ocid:` is host-specific:** `/commit/` is GitHub's path and other hosts differ, so this is a display convenience, and `ochid:` stays what the tools resolve. The name is also one letter from `ochid:`, so I'd consider something more distinct, like `ocommit:`.

**What I'd do:** adopt it for local cycles, and change this ladder so **commit and init stamp a URL-shaped ochid** stays for `-s b` and `init`, with a new rung, **land stamps a local cycle's trailers**. `ocid:` gets its own rung after that, because of the At rest change it forces. The agent `@` still isn't committed until land, so keeping today's trailers on the opening and this rung does no harm.

The readers rung doesn't depend on this decision and is still waiting on your review.

The plain version: leave rungs without trailers until land, commit the agent first, then stamp every work commit with links to it. It works well as long as the agent commit never changes after land, and today it does.

That settles your side of it, but the tool does the same squash on its own, so it needs a fix too. Today's land output shows it: `push agent: squash @ -> @- + push main`, then `squash-push: squashing @ -> @-...`.

The session keeps writing to the agent `@` while a land runs. If the agent commit is made, the work commits get stamped, and then the push folds in whatever arrived since, the agent SHA changes and every `ocid:` is wrong the moment it's published.

So the land has to push the agent commit exactly as stamped, leaving anything new in `@`. `vc-x1 push` needs the same treatment when a partner is already committed: it shouldn't fold into a commit that a stamped `ocid:` names.

**What follows from dropping the squash**
- **At rest:** item 2, your `squash-push -s a`, comes out of the rules. "Clean" then means the work `@` is empty, and acquaint already doesn't treat the agent `@` as a finding. That goes in the v0.3.1 proposal.
- **The session's tail:** it stays uncommitted until the next cycle's agent commit, which picks it up. The transcript of a land stays local until then, so a lost machine would lose it, but as you say it's only bookkeeping.
- **`squash-push -s a` itself:** it can stay as a command for anyone who asks for it, but it would be dangerous once `ocid:` exists, so it joins the candidates for the `--yes` guard.

**Decisions I'm treating as made, unless you say otherwise:**
- You stop running `squash-push -s a`.
- Rungs carry no trailer until land, and land stamps them.
- The ladder gains **land stamps a local cycle's trailers** and an `ocid:` rung, with the no-fold change inside the first.

I'll write these into the ladder and Deliberation when I start the next rung, so the readers rung stays as you're reviewing it.

from your PoV and you then remain quiet/silent. The code waits a few seconds and does everything to land and push

Thoughts only

It's a good fit, and it also solves the transcript's last mile: the agent commit would hold the session right up to the land, including my final word, so there's no tail left behind. It also matches the hard stop after the final push, because the land really is the last thing that happens and I'm already quiet.

**Adjustments I'd make**
1. **Check first, then detach.** Every refusal runs in the foreground: the partner check, tree check, lease and conflicts. That way I can still report a refused land to you, and only the mechanical part goes to the background.
2. **Wait for quiet rather than a fixed few seconds.** Transcript writes after a tool result have no guaranteed timing. I'd watch the agent directory until nothing has changed for a few seconds, with a ceiling.
3. **Keep the no-fold rule anyway.** A late write can still land after the agent commit, so it stays in `@` for the next cycle. The rule costs little and makes the timing harmless rather than just unlikely.

**Problems it creates**
- **Nobody sees the outcome.** This is the biggest one, because the process is pushing to remotes with me silent, so a failed push could go unnoticed. You're right about the output. You've used this technique and I haven't, and my claim was a guess about the harness. The detach rung can just try it, and the log file stays only for when you've walked away.

The actor is the better long-term shape, because several problems from the spawned process go away:

- **Collisions:** one actor handles one message at a time, so concurrent writes get queued rather than needing a lock, as long as they all go through it.
- **Outcome:** the result is a reply, so "land finished or failed" has a defined form and place.
- **What comes next:** a checking agent or a restart becomes another message sent when the land is done, which is your earlier idea with nothing extra to build.
- **Waiting for quiet:** the actor can watch the agent directory as part of handling the land.

**Questions it raises**
- **The actor replaces itself:** a land ends by installing a new `vc-x1`, so a long-running actor would still be running the old code until it restarts. It needs to exit and restart cleanly after an install, and a message sent by a newer client than the actor needs a defined answer.
- **Who keeps it running:** a daemon brings starting, stale instances, crashes and one per workspace. I'd avoid that at first: the first message starts the actor, and it exits when its mailbox is empty. That gives the same interface with no lifetime to manage.
- **Transport:** a file mailbox in a gitignored directory is the simplest choice and works on every platform, and it survives a crash, which a socket doesn't.
- **Authority:** any local process could send it a `land`. Your go still has to come through me and the rules, so the actor doesn't replace approvals.
- **Bypasses:** raw `jj` never goes through the actor, so a rule is still needed for that.
- **Replies mustn't wake me unasked:** a reply that wakes me would write to the transcript and undo the quiet the land waits for, so replies should wait until you speak or I ask.

**How I'd sequence it:** the spawned land is already a one-message actor that starts, handles the message and exits. So I'd write the detach rung with the land as a message handed to a function, and let the actor grow out of that without changing the land's code. The actor itself is too big for this cycle, so I'd file it as a Todo, **vc-x1 is an actor**, folding in **a finished land starts what comes next** rather than filing both.

content.text:
That removes the lifetime questions, and I withdraw my suggestion of an actor that starts on demand. Starting it, keeping it alive and restarting it are all the user's, for example through systemd.

Three small things are left on the client side:

- **No service running:** the client fails at once and says so, rather than queueing a message nothing will read. Nothing should appear to have landed when it hasn't.
- **Version mismatch:** a land ends by installing a new binary, and a running service keeps the old code until it's restarted. Restarting is the user's job, but the client and service should compare versions and report a mismatch, so a stale service is visible.
- **Fallback:** the land stays an ordinary function, so it can still run in the foreground without the service, as on a machine that hasn't installed it.

I'd file the Todo with that framing: **vc-x1 is an actor**, a user-installed service that the client sends asynchronous messages to.

(wink + agent, 2026-10-30) `vc-x1` stamps `/.claude/<chid>` on every agent trailer whatever the
directory is called, from the constant `OCHID_BOT_LABEL` in `src/desc_helpers.rs`, so this workspace's

- A renamed repo leaves its trailers stale, and rewriting them rewrites published history, so a small
  mapping of old URL to new in `.vc-config.md` is the likely answer. A deleted or private repo is the
  link rot the design note accepts: the code stays authoritative and only the context is lost.

### vc-x1 is an actor

(wink + agent, 2026-10-30) `vc-x1` becomes a service the user installs, and a client sends it
asynchronous messages. From **feat: ochid trailers are URLs**, where a Land is to run after the agent
goes quiet, so the transcript it commits is whole: first as a detached process, wink's technique
from the olden days, and then as a message to the actor.

- Its lifetime is the user's: the service is installed, started, and restarted by them, systemd or
  the like, and no agent manages it.
- One actor handles one message at a time, so writes through it queue rather than collide. Raw `jj`
  never goes through it, so that stays a rule.
- A reply is the outcome, so "land finished or failed" has a defined form and place. A reply does not
  wake the agent, since waking it writes to the transcript the Land is waiting to go quiet.
- The client:
  - no service running fails at once and says so, rather than queueing a message nothing reads
  - client and service compare versions and report a mismatch, since a Land installs a new binary
    and a running service keeps the old code until restarted
  - the Land stays an ordinary function, so it runs in the foreground with no service.
- Authority: any local process can send a message, so the user's go still comes through the agent and
  the rules.
- What a finished Land can start, by another message:
  - an agent that checks `main` in both repos, the deleted bookmarks, and the installed version,
    read-only and outside the dual-repo protocol
  - a restart of the agent for the next step, automating [Close-out](AGENTS.md#close-out) step 7,
    which begins with an acquaint and inherits no approval, so a restart is no unattended chain of
    pushes.
- Open: the transport, we think a file mailbox in a gitignored directory, which survives a crash and
  works on every platform **vc-x1 runs on Windows and macOS** names.

### feat: ochid trailers are URLs

Picked from `## Todo`, filed the same day, wink's call (2026-10-30).

#### Problem

(wink + agent, 2026-10-30) `vc-x1` stamps `/.claude/<chid>` on every agent trailer whatever the
directory is called, from the constant `OCHID_BOT_LABEL` in `src/desc_helpers.rs`, so this workspace's
`.agent-session` is never named, and nothing in a published commit says where its partner lives.
Anyone cloning just the work-repo can't resolve the agent side. Wink's decision: fix it correctly,
the trailer a URL in both directions. Folds in **ochid values may be URLs** and **ochid: agent-repo
location qualifier**, and the ochid-label bullet of **The docs and the code say .claude where they
mean the agent-repo directory**. The design is sketched in [Per-user bot repos via URL-shaped
ochid](notes/forks-multi-user.md#per-user-bot-repos-via-url-shaped-ochid).

- The form, the repo's URL and the change id:
  - `ochid: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1.agent-session#qrxovvvqxnrq`
  - `ochid: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1#uzkpltwmukvx`
- The change id and not a SHA: a SHA changes on every squash and rewrite, and a clone keeps change
  ids. So the URL says where to look and `vc-x1` resolves the rest, and it is no clickable link to
  the commit, GitHub knowing only SHAs.
- Resolved locally first: a URL matching a repo of this workspace by its `origin` needs no network,
  and only a URL matching nothing fetches.
- The URL is read from `origin` at commit time and normalized to https, so ssh and https clones stamp
  the same value. Whether `[remote] agent-repo` in `.vc-config.md`, which already names the
  agent-repo's remote, should supply it is to be decided.
- No remote yet, `init`'s cross-links made before the remotes and `adopt` or a local-path remote:
  a fallback is defined, and we think it is the path form, `/.agent-session/<chid>`, the configured
  directory rather than the constant. A `file://` path is no answer, being one machine's.
- A renamed repo leaves its trailers stale, and rewriting them rewrites published history, so a small
  mapping of old URL to new in `.vc-config.md` is the likely answer. A deleted or private repo is the
  link rot the design note accepts: the code stays authoritative and only the context is lost.
- Published trailers stay valid and are never rewritten: `/.claude/<id>` and `/<id>` keep resolving.
  Today `validate_ochid` compares the prefix exactly, so it and `fix-desc` learn this, or they flag
  or rewrite all of history.
- Readers before writers: one rung teaches every reader the URL form, a later one stamps it, so no
  build writes a form it cannot read, across the family's repos on different versions too. The
  readers: `extract_bare_id`, `validate_ochid`, `fix-desc`, `lookup::partner`, the `dr-1` fixture,
  and push's pending-partner check.
- A cycle's own rungs carry the URL too, wink's call (2026-10-30), by the bends in the Deliberation.
- `jj.md`'s trailer section and the rules naming `/.claude/` follow, so **agent-files(proposal):

message.content: Now here is an interesting question, should we update the ladder for the older commits, we obviously can, my reaction is not unless it to correct a "significant" error,  but "significant" is in the eye of the beholder, so no explicit rule against it.

content.text:
I agree: leave older commits' ladders alone unless the error is significant, and don't add a rule. The rules already lean that way: the record is "revised as rungs land", with no backfill, and a late finding about a closed cycle is recorded where it's found. Each commit's ladder is the plan as it stood then, and seeing that plan change is part of the value, as today's rungs show.

Rewriting costs more than it looks, even while local. The trailer rewrites touched descriptions only, so every tree stayed as validated. Changing a ladder changes a tree, which means that tree was never validated, and because later rungs edit the same lines of `zDOING.md`, the rebase would likely conflict.

If you want a yardstick for "significant" without a rule, I'd use this: would the old text mislead someone who reads only that commit, in a way the later history doesn't correct? A leaked secret or a wrong acceptance result would qualify. A rung that was renamed, added or reordered wouldn't.

**We have a real case to try it on.** The opening's committed Deliberation says the `/.claude/` trailers were "wink's acceptance", which you never actually said, and it's wrong about what those trailers ended up being. The next rung's record corrects it, and that correction is on the same line of history, so by that yardstick I'd leave it.

I've added that to the v0.3.1 proposal as **A local cycle's record may be reworked**. It's uncommitted, and `AGENTS.md` itself stays as it is until the proposal runs:

- While a cycle's work commits are local and its agent `@` is neither committed nor pushed, an earlier commit's record may be reworked.
- By default it's unnecessary, and it's permissible when the error is significant. "Significant" is left to judgment, with no test fixed.
- A reworked tree gets validated again, since no validation saw it.
- Once published, **Never amended** and **Re-describing** apply as they do now.

**A correction:** I misquoted "no backfill" in my last message. In `AGENTS.md` it means something narrower: a rung carries no `[[N]]` placeholder, no SHA and no version. So it never ruled out what you're describing, and the definitive-sounding line was my paraphrase rather than the rule. I left it unchanged. The rules that do bear on this are **Never amended** (closed cycles) and **Re-describing** (published commits), and neither stops rework on a local cycle. So the new section adds a permission that was missing rather than relaxing existing language.

The `origin` rung is ready to start on your go.

content.text:
I agree, and I'd make it the default, but only once it has landed once. So far we've made two local commits with hand-written trailers. The land that stamps them doesn't exist yet, and that's the part the whole idea depends on.

**Why it deserves to be the default**
- **Fewer stops:** the reviews stay, but approval per push reduces to one go at the land. That's where the real decision is.
- **Free rework:** nothing published can name a rung, so reshaping a ladder costs nothing, which is exactly how today went.
- **No dangling links:** the agent commit comes first and stamps everything, with clickable `ocid:` links and one trailer per rung back from the agent.

**What it changes in the rules**
- **Sections it changes:** Opening step 2, the per-rung flow's step 9, Committing vs pushing, At rest and **Approval per push** all get rewritten.
- **In the proposal:** **A local commit pair before every push** gets replaced, since rungs no longer make a pair. **Every cycle starts with `commit --opening`** still holds, except that the bookmark stays local.

**Risks to settle in the proposal**
1. **One machine:** this is the biggest. You work on 3900x and fwlaptop, and a local cycle can't move between them or survive losing the disk. It needs an answer, probably an explicit backup push of the work bookmark that names nothing as landed. That runs into the rule that what's published names nothing unpublished, and into the land rewriting those commits, so it has to be designed rather than assumed.
2. **Shared repos:** **Cycles in a shared repo, by fork and pull request** needs a branch pushed before anything lands, so the stamping and the publishing have to be separate steps. If the land is built as one lump, that work gets harder later.
3. **One large agent commit:** the whole cycle's transcript sits in a single commit, which gets close to the size limit that **fix: snapshot fails on a file the size limit refused** dealt with. It also makes `lookup` less precise per rung. Long cycles are where this would bite.
4. **The old form:** I wouldn't retire publishing per rung yet. A cycle someone wants visible while it runs still needs it, and the commands exist anyway. So this becomes the default, not the only form.

**What I'd do:**
- Add **A cycle stays local until its Land** to the v0.3.1 proposal now, marked on trial, with the risks above as open items.
- Make it the cycle of record at this cycle's closing, if the land works.

Should I add it now?

The plain version: yes, this should become the normal way to run a cycle, but write it in as a trial until this cycle's land proves it, and solve the one-machine problem before relying on it.

input.new_string:
A repo now has a canonical URL, and a trailer's URL is checked against it, while nothing stamps one
yet.

- `url::canonical_repo_url` turns `https`, `http`, `ssh`, and scp-style remotes into
  `https://<host>/<path>`, so ssh and https clones agree. It drops a user, password, and port, since
  the value goes into published commits, and a trailing `/` and `.git`. A local path and `file://`
  have none.
- `OchidForms`, by `ochid_forms_for`, is what a trailer naming a repo may be: the published label,
  the path form by the directory's own name, `/.agent-session/`, the fallback for a repo with no URL,
  and the URL from its `origin`.
- `validate_ochid` checks against it, so a URL naming another repo is now wrong, in any spelling of
  the right one being accepted, and with no hosted `origin` to compare a URL passes on its ID.
- `fix-desc` reports a wrong URL and does not rewrite it, since a renamed repo would otherwise have
  all its history rewritten. The mapping of old URL to new stays open, not in this cycle.

I've renamed the next rung to **feat: commit and init stamp a URL-shaped ochid and ocid**, and the `origin` rung (`-2`) is ready for your review. Full validation passes and it isn't committed yet.

**What the `origin` rung does**
- **Canonical URL:** `https`, `http`, `ssh` and scp-style remotes all become `https://<host>/<path>`. It drops any user, password and port, since the value goes into published commits. Local paths and `file://` have none.
- **Accepted forms:** a trailer may be the published label, the path form by the directory's name (`/.agent-session/`, the no-remote fallback), or the URL from `origin`.
- **`validate-desc`:** a URL naming another repo now fails, while any spelling of the right one passes. With no hosted `origin`, it checks only the id.
- **`fix-desc`:** it reports a wrong URL and doesn't rewrite it, since a renamed repo would otherwise have all its history rewritten. Mapping old URLs to new is left open.
- **Real repos:** `vc-x1-dev`, built before the last test was added, passes the opening and readers rung against the actual `origin`, plus two older `/.claude/` trailers.

**One thing to settle on the `-3` rung:** at commit time there's no agent SHA for `ocid:` yet, so I'd stamp the `.../commit/xxxx` placeholder there, and the land rung fills it in. That works for local cycles. A `-s b` commit in the publish-per-rung form has a harder case, because later folds change the agent SHA, so its `ocid:` wouldn't stay accurate. I'd have `-s b` and `init` stamp only `ochid:`, unless you want otherwise.

content.text:
Yes, this composition is clean, and it gives the land rung its structure: `--closing` makes a commit and `push` publishes it, on each side, with the agent first so its SHA exists when the work side is stamped. It also fits your earlier `--closing -sa` decision and **commit works at every scope**.

**Your two forms aren't quite equivalent when something fails**
- **Form 1** (`--closing -sa`, `--closing -sw`, `push -sa`, `push -sw`): nothing is published until both closings exist. If the work closing fails, you've lost nothing and can just retry.
- **Form 2** (`land -sa`, then `land -sw`): the agent commit is already public when the work closing is attempted. A failure there leaves its `ochid:` lines on `origin` naming work commits that aren't published.

So I'd build `land -sb` as form 1. Form 2 stays valid by hand, for when you want the steps separate.

**What it needs to work**
1. **The agent commit names a closing that doesn't exist yet.** `--closing -sa` runs first, but its `ochid:` lines include the work closing. That's solvable: the closing keeps the work `@`'s change id, which is why `commit` can already stamp it before making the merge. So the id is known ahead of time.
2. **Which step stamps the work rungs:** I'd put it in `--closing -sw`, which writes `ochid:` and `ocid:` on every commit from opening to closing, trees unchanged.
3. **`land -sX` has jobs beyond `push`:** today's land also fast-forwards the trunk and deletes the cycle's bookmark. Those go on the work side's step. For a trunk move on the agent side, `push -sa` already moves its `main`.
4. **Rerunning has to be safe:** each step should see its work is already done and skip it, which also covers a land whose closing was made earlier. `push` already works this way, so a failed land resumes by running it again.
5. **Alone, each side is dangerous:**
   - `land -sw` with no agent commit would publish `xxxx` placeholders and an `ochid:` naming nothing.
   - `land -sa` alone publishes `ochid:` lines naming unpublished work commits.

   Both become errors unless `--yes` is given, unless the other side is already done. That's what makes form 2 work without `--yes`, if `land -sa` is allowed as the first half of it. These are good first entries for your "dangerous" list.

I'll write this into the **land stamps a local cycle's trailers** rung when we reach it.

The `origin` rung (`-2`) is still waiting on your review.

The plain version: `land -sb` is agent closing, work closing, push agent, push work. Your composition holds, and doing both closings before either push makes failure harmless.

Yes, it should, and I've filed that as **The exit code says what failed**, just above **vc-x1 is an actor**. Today nearly every failure exits 1, clap's usage errors exit 2, and only `agent-files diff` returns its own code.

It matters more with what we've just designed:
- **The composed land:** the code can say whether the agent closing, the work closing, the agent push or the work push failed, so a retry knows what was already done.
- **Agent and actor:** I and a future actor would act on a code rather than parsing a message.

The Todo's first cut also separates these cases:
- refused before anything moved, versus failed partway
- a guard `--yes` would pass, versus an error it wouldn't
- a push rejected by a lease, versus a network failure

**Decisions in it:**
- The codes are a documented table, stable once published.
- The error type carries its code, so a command returns one by what happened and not from a string.
- The message stays the explanation.
- Codes stay under 126, because the shell reserves the ones above.
- **status prints a verdict per repo and exits with a bit per side** becomes part of that table.

It's a separate cycle and doesn't change the `origin` rung, though the land rung could use it when it arrives. This Todo entry goes into the `origin` rung's commit too, alongside the proposal and ladder edits.

content.text:
That shape works well, and I've added it to the Todo. A code reads like `0x34`: stage 3, type 4.

**It fits the shell neatly**
- **Range:** 0x7E and up belong to the shell (126, 127, and 128 plus a signal), so the upper digit runs 0 to 7. A set top bit always means killed, never one of ours.
- **Stage 0 means nothing moved:** that gives you "refused before anything moved" without a separate type. Today's 1 and clap's 2 also keep their meanings as `0x01` and `0x02`.

**Decisions in the Todo**
- **Stages belong to each command:** `land -s b` would have the agent closing as 1, the work closing as 2, the agent push as 3, the work push as 4, and so on, documented with the command.
- **Types are global:** one digit means the same thing everywhere, such as a guard `--yes` would pass, a rejected lease, the network or a conflict.

**Two open items**
- **`status` collision:** its planned exit of 1, 2 or 3 per side is a verdict, and it would clash with stage 0's types, so one of them has to move.
- **Stage count:** eight stages may be short for a long composed command. `land -s b` fits, but it's worth checking when the land rung is written.

content.text:
Today `--no-push` is correct everywhere except the opening, so there's only one gap. From the trials:

| Form | `--no-push` |
|---|---|
| rung | works |
| `--closing` | works, stays local |
| `--opening` | **still pushes the bookmark**, unless you add `--skip remote` |
| `--closing --land` | refused by clap; **commit works at every scope** plans your local land |

As planned, it wouldn't be fixed until **commit works at every scope, and --local keeps it on the machine**, a later cycle. That's too late for something **A cycle stays local until its Land** relies on, because forgetting `--skip remote` publishes a bookmark you meant to keep local.

The fix is small: the opening's push check should also respect `--no-push` and `[commit] push = false`. I recommend adding a rung now, before the stamping work: **fix: --no-push keeps the opening's bookmark local**, version `-3`. The later rungs move up by one, and the Todo drops that item.

The local land, `--land --local`, stays in that later cycle, since this cycle lands by `land -s b` anyway.

Should I add that rung now, or leave it in the Todo? Your go adds it and starts it.

Whether `vc-x1 commit` pushes what it commits in the same invocation, as `vc-x1 push` would after
it. True is the default, every commit published as soon as it is made: `--no-push` keeps one commit
local and `--push` pushes one when the key is false. A commit with `--no-advance` pushes only with
`--push`, since its bookmark was left where it was. Owned by the work side because the commits are
the work repo's.

```toml
[commit.push]
homes = ["workspace-code"]
kind = "bool"
doc = "Default for commit: push what it commits, `--no-push` / `--push` override"
used-by = "vc-x1 commit --push / --no-push"
default = true
Commit the working copies as a rung's pair, one commit per repo of a dual workspace, each stamped
with the other's change id, and push it in the same invocation. The diff and the description are
reviewed before the commit, so what is pushed is what was reviewed, and `--no-push` keeps a commit
local for a look at it by `vc-x1 show -s both @-` before `push`. Both change ids are
known before either commit is made, since a jj commit keeps the working copy's change id, so each
b`, a plain repo by `push -s p`, and an agent commit by publishing the agent repo's `main`. The diff
and the description are reviewed before the commit, so what is pushed is what was reviewed.
`--no-push` keeps one commit local, for a look at it before `vc-x1 push`, `[commit] push = false`
makes that the default, and `--push` overrides the key. A commit with `--no-advance` pushes only
with `--push`, since its bookmark was left where it was.

Whether `vc-x1 commit` pushes what it commits in the same invocation, as `vc-x1 push` would after
it. True is the default, every commit published as soon as it is made: `--no-push` keeps one commit
local and `--push` pushes one when the key is false. A commit with `--no-advance` pushes only with
`--push`, since its bookmark was left where it was. Owned by the work side because the commits are
the work repo's.

Full validation passes, so the `-3` rung is ready for review, and yes: `--local` should be the default, with publishing always asked for by `--push`.

**Your idea, `--local` by default**
- **Why it's right:** a local commit can be undone or reworked, and a push can't easily be taken back, so the safe choice should be the one you get by doing nothing. It's also the whole of **A cycle stays local until its Land**, with no flag to forget.
- **Existing message:** a commit already prints `kept local, vc-x1 push publishes it`, so someone expecting a push is told straight away.

**What it would change**
- **`--land`:** it keeps pushing on its own, since landing is the explicit request to publish. `--land --local` stays the separate local land in the Todo.
- **`[commit] push`:** I'd remove the key. "Always require `--push`" means there's no workspace setting that changes what a bare `commit` does, so the behaviour is the same everywhere. `--local` and `--no-push` stay accepted, as flags that state the default.
- **Things relying on today's default:**
  - `support/fixtures/build-dr-1.py`, which needs `--push` added
  - the per-rung flow's step 9, which goes in the v0.3.1 proposal
  - the README and `vc-config.md`
  - the test helper, which gets simpler because it no longer has to force `--local`

I'd do this as part of this rung, because it's the same flag and the same few lines, and renaming it to **fix: commit stays local unless --push asks** would cover it. Removing a config key and changing a default also has to be stated clearly to anyone else using `vc-x1`, so it belongs in the proposal too.

**The rung as it stands**
- **`--local`:** now the flag, with `--no-push` as a visible alias.
- **`--opening`:** its bookmark follows `--local` and `[commit] push`, and the new test covers the flag, the alias, the key and `--push`.
- **Behaviour change:** `commit --opening` with no `--no-push` now pushes the opening as well as the bookmark. That wasn't a mistake, but it was a surprise when I hit it: the old `--opening --no-push`, bookmark published and opening local, no longer exists. If you ever want it, it's `--opening --no-advance`, which leaves the bookmark at the start.
- **Failures on the way:** six opening tests failed because the helper sets `--local`, which the old opening ignored. I changed them to ask for the push, and they then needed new assertions for what gets published. The seventh, the config model, needed regenerating for the renamed flag.

Your go adds the default change to this rung and renames it, and I'd stop for your review again before committing.

content.text:
I like this even better, and it makes the model simpler: **`commit` never publishes unless you say `--push`, and `--land` becomes a local operation too.** That retracts what I said a moment ago about `--land` pushing on its own, and `--land --local` stops being a special case.

**What it buys**
- **Your composition:** closing on each side, then publish as a separate step, is now just what the commands do. Nothing is public until both closings exist.
- **Test before publishing:** `main` moves locally, you install and try the binary, and only then push. That's what **Land validates and installs before the main push** asked for, and it should remove the need for the candidate-binary flow in v0.3.1.
- **No approvals for local work:** rungs and land run freely, and all the risk sits in one flag.

**"Requires approval" needs a mechanism**
- **`--yes` alone proves nothing for an agent:** I can type `--yes` as easily as anything else, and `vc-x1` can't tell who ran it.
- **The hook can enforce it:** `bash-allow.sh` already decides which commands skip the permission prompt. It could send anything publishing to Claude Code's permission prompt, so you approve it there. That's a real gate, and it also works without a terminal.
- **What `--yes` then means:** for a person or a script it skips `vc-x1`'s own prompt, and I'd have the hook ask anyway when an agent runs it. If you want to waive that, it's a setting of yours and not something I decide per command.

**Loose ends**
- **The other publishing commands:** `vc-x1 push`, `squash-push` and `land` all publish too. If only `commit --push` is gated, `commit` followed by `push` walks around it. All of them need the same gate.
- **`vc-x1 land`:** it should follow the same rule, local unless `--push`, or it would disagree with `commit --land`.
- **A forgotten push:** local `main` sits ahead of `origin`, which `sync` and the acquaint look already report, so it can't go unnoticed for long. The bookmark deletion just stays local until the push.

**How I'd split it**

content.text:
The `-3` rung, now **fix: commit stays local unless --push asks**, is ready for review. Full validation passes, and it isn't committed. A dry run with `vc-x1-dev` confirms a bare `commit` now prints `kept local` and pushes nothing.

**What changed**
- **Default:** a bare `vc-x1 commit` publishes nothing, including the opening's bookmark. `--push` is the only thing that publishes.
- **`--local` and `--no-push`:** both still accepted, and they just state the default.
- **`[commit] push`:** removed. `commit` no longer reads it, and `validate-config` reports one left in a config as an unknown key.
- **Docs and fixtures:** the help text, README, `vc-config.md` and regenerated model are updated, and `build-dr-1.py` now passes `--push`. `jj.md` still says `--no-push`, which remains true through the alias, until v0.3.1 runs.
- **Proposal:** v0.3.1 gains **Only push publishes**, with your two-line rule and the open approval mechanism.

**Things to check**
- **Publishing only a cycle's name:** `--opening --no-advance --push` publishes the bookmark at the start and keeps the opening local. I kept this so the old mode has one remaining form. It's my call rather than something you asked for, and it's easy to drop.
- **`--land` still pushes:** that's deliberate for now, and it changes in the land rung along with `vc-x1 land`. So until then, `commit --closing --land` is still a publish, and it needs your go.
- **Other agent-file text:** the per-rung flow's step 9 still says `commit` pushes. That goes with the proposal, so `AGENTS.md` is out of date until it runs.

**Failures along the way:** eight tests failed across these two passes, and all of them relied on the old default:
- The six opening tests needed new assertions for what gets published.
- Two land tests had setup commits that now have to ask for `--push`.

No other tests needed changes for the default, and the renamed flag only meant regenerating the model file.

content.text:
Yes to both, as a Todo for later.

**`--no-move`:** I agree. It uses the same word as the command, and "advance" sounds as if the bookmark can only go forward. It's also a cheap rename, following the pattern `vc-x1` already uses for retired flags: the old name is refused with a message naming the new one.

**`bookmark`:** grouping them is right, but I'd use subcommands rather than flags: `vc-x1 bookmark create|delete|move`.
- **Each verb takes different options:** `move` needs a target, `delete` has `--skip`-style sides, and `create` needs a revision. With flags on one command, the help lists them all together, and clap has to reject the invalid combinations one by one. Subcommands get this for free, with help per verb.
- **It matches what's nearby:** `jj bookmark create|delete|move` has the same shape, which fits **push follows jj** and **agent-files(proposal): vc-x1 is the interface, jj the engine**. **Nest the validate and fix commands** and `agent-files copy|diff` go the same way. The "every argument is a flag" rule is about a command's arguments, not its verbs, so this doesn't conflict with it.

**A consequence from today's rule:** if only `push` publishes, the `bookmark` verbs should be local too. `delete-bookmark` removes the bookmark on `origin` as well today, so it would change to deleting locally, with the remote side taken care of by `--push`. `move-bookmark` needs the same check, which I haven't done. That also answers the open question about a land deleting a published bookmark.

I'd file it as one Todo, **bookmark takes create, delete, and move**, next to **commit works at every scope**, with `--no-move` included. I haven't filed it, since you asked for thoughts only.

The `-3` rung is still waiting on your review.

Commit the working copies as a rung's pair, one commit per repo of a
dual workspace, each stamped with the other's change id, and with
--push publish it in the same invocation, as `vc-x1 push` would.

The diff and the description are reviewed before the commit, so the
push publishes what was reviewed. It stays on the machine unless
--push asks, for a look at it by `vc-x1 show -s both @-` before
`vc-x1 push`. --local says so outright.

-r REV is the commit the description is for: `@` by default,

A bare commit publishes what it makes, and --no-push leaves the
opening's bookmark to be pushed anyway, so keeping a cycle local takes
flags that are easy to forget, and forgetting one publishes it.

bookmark included, --local and its alias --no-push say so outright, and
the [commit] push key goes, so no workspace changes what a bare commit
does. See details in zDOING.md.

message.content: How do I  make a "local" test repo so  I can test with a repo but the repo is local?

content.text:
Use `init` with a local directory as the remote, which is what my trials did:

```bash
mkdir -p tmp/remotes-a
cd tmp
vc-x1-dev init --target ./a --repo local=$PWD/remotes-a
cd a
```

That gives you a full dual workspace: work repo, agent repo in `.agent-session`, and bare repos in `remotes-a` acting as `origin`. Pushes, land and `git ls-remote origin` all work with no network.

**Things to know**
- **One remote directory per workspace:** the bare repos came out as `remote-work.git` and `remote-work.agent-session.git` whatever the target was called, so a second `init` in the same directory is refused with "already exists". That naming looks like a bug, so it may be worth a line in the Todo.
- **`~/.claude/projects`:** `init` also creates a Claude Code symlink there. To keep your real one clean, set `HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` to a scratch directory, and give that `HOME` a `.config/jj/config.toml` with your name and email. `tmp/wflow.sh` has the whole setup at the top, and running it is a working example, though its workspaces land beside the script.
- **Inside the repo:** I ran these trials under `/tmp`, not `./tmp`. The workspace has its own `.vc-config.md`, so commands should find it first, but if `init` fails partway a command could find this repo's config instead. Check that you're in the right place before anything that writes.
- **URL trailers:** a local path has no canonical URL, so a local workspace can't exercise that form end to end. Once the stamping rung lands, these repos get the `/.agent-session/<chid>` fallback, and a URL trailer can only be checked by writing one by hand. Testing a real URL stamp needs a repo with a hosted `origin`.
- **Which binary:** `vc-x1` is still 0.85.17, so use `vc-x1-dev` to get this cycle's behavior, such as `commit` staying local by default.

content.text:
No, advancing is the default and `--no-advance` is the opt-out. A commit moves the line's nearest bookmark up to it, and in your test repo there's no cycle bookmark, so the nearest one is `main`. It moved locally only, since nothing was pushed, and `origin` still has the old `main`.

It did reveal a gap, though. The rules say `main` advances only when a cycle lands, but a bare `commit` with no opening moves it anyway, and the new local default doesn't change that. The commit is made, the bookmark stays put, and it prints a line saying so, pointing at `--opening` or `--land`. Moving the trunk is then only ever the land's job, which matches the two-line rule: `commit` makes commits, `land` moves the trunk, and `push` publishes. Other bookmarks keep advancing as they do now.

The cost is that a plain repo or a throwaway project like yours, worked directly on `main`, would need `land` or an explicit `--bookmark main`. ```

" closing" belongs on a separate closing commit, when there are rungs in between. A ladder gets three kinds of title:

```
feat: rust helloworld opening
feat: a rung
feat: rust helloworld closing
```

The rules already work this way. **Cycle shape** says a single-step cycle is titled with the bare cycle title, and v0.3.1's **A cycle's shape is its branch's commit count** says the bare title replaces the opening's. So the title itself tells a reader which kind of cycle it was, and "closing" with no matching "opening" in the history would suggest a ladder that never existed.

- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:google-workspace: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.
- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
